definition_zh: 中心；中央；中心机构；使集中
definition_en: the middle point of something, a place or building where an activity is based, or to place something in the middle
core_image: 圆规尖脚扎下的那一点，四周等距
scene: 广场四周都是店铺。 A fountain stands at the center of the square.
sceneCN: 这里 center 指「中心」（第 1 个义项：广场的中央位置）；句意是广场中央立着一座喷泉。

senses.title: The middle point
senses.definition: the middle point of an area, circle or object, equally distant from the edges
senses.definitionCN: 区域、圆或物体的中点，与边缘等距
senses.example: There is a table in the center of the room.
senses.exampleCN: 房间中央有一张桌子。
senses.why: The Greek source was the fixed point of a compass, and that point is always the middle.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语源词是圆规固定不动的那个点，而那个点永远是中央。

senses.title: A place for an activity
senses.definition: a building or area where a particular activity or service is based
senses.definitionCN: 某项活动或服务所在的建筑或区域
senses.example: She works at a health center.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一家健康中心工作。
senses.why: A place where people gather for one purpose becomes the centre of that activity.
senses.whyCN: 人们为同一目的聚集的地方，就成了这项活动的中心。

senses.title: To place in the middle
senses.definition: to put something in the middle, or to make one thing the main focus
senses.definitionCN: 把某物放在中间，或使某事物成为主要焦点
senses.example: The discussion centered on pay.
senses.exampleCN: 讨论集中在薪酬问题上。
senses.why: The verb reverses the noun: to centre is to make something the middle point.
senses.whyCN: 动词是名词的反向使用：使集中就是让某物成为中点。

intro.en: Center goes back to a Greek word for a sharp point, the fixed leg of a pair of compasses.
intro.cn: center 可追到希腊语中表示尖点的词，即圆规固定不动的那个脚。

items.en: Kentron meant a sharp point, a goad, and the fixed point of a compass.
items.cn: 希腊语 kentron 指尖点、刺棒，以及圆规的定点。

items.en: Centrum borrowed the Greek word for the middle point of a circle.
items.cn: 拉丁语 centrum 借入该希腊词，指圆的中心点。

items.en: Centre carried the geometric sense into medieval French.
items.cn: 古法语 centre 把几何义带入中世纪法语。

items.en: English centre names the middle of a circle and then of any space.
items.cn: 中古英语 centre 先指圆心，后指任何空间的中央。

items.en: American spelling drops the -re, and the word extends to shopping centres and centres of research.
items.cn: 美式拼写去掉 -re，词义扩展到购物中心与研究中心。

note.en: The look-alike group includes the British spelling and the derived forms, while the meaning group lists other middle words.
note.cn: 形近组包含英式拼写与派生形式，近义组列出其他表示中部的词。

entries.definition: the British spelling of the same word
entries.definitionCN: 同一词的英式拼写

entries.definition: in the middle, or most important
entries.definitionCN: 位于中央的，或最重要的

entries.definition: a person with middle political views
entries.definitionCN: 持中间政治立场的人

entries.definition: the point equally far from two sides
entries.definitionCN: 与两边等距的点

entries.definition: the central part of something
entries.definitionCN: 事物的中心部分

entries.definition: the central point of activity
entries.definitionCN: 活动的中心点

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the compass-point root, the -al and -ist endings and the shopping phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用圆规定点词根、-al 与 -ist 词尾以及购物搭配。

normal.en: A centre is the point where the compass needle stands still, the one fixed place.
normal.cn: 中心就是圆规针尖不动的那一点，唯一固定的位置。

normal.en: Central and centrist keep the same root and shift it to an adjective and a person.
normal.cn: central 与 centrist 保留同一词根，分别转为形容词与人。

normal.en: Centre in British spelling and center in American spelling differ by two letters.
normal.cn: 英式 centre 与美式 center 只差两个字母的位置。

normal.en: Center on means to make one subject the fixed point of a discussion.
normal.cn: center on 意为让一个话题成为讨论的定点。

normal.en: Center of attention is the same picture applied to people in a room.
normal.cn: center of attention 把同一画面用到房间里的人身上。

abstract.en: Picture a compass leg pressed into paper while the other draws a circle.
abstract.cn: 想象圆规一只脚扎进纸里，另一只脚画出圆圈。

abstract.en: Picture a fountain in the middle of a crowded square.
abstract.cn: 想象拥挤广场正中的一座喷泉。

abstract.en: Picture everyone in a room turning toward one speaker.
abstract.cn: 想象满屋人都转向同一位发言者。

examples.en: The hotel is in the center of town.
examples.cn: 这家旅馆位于镇中心。

examples.en: The new center will help young families.
examples.cn: 这个新中心将帮助年轻家庭。

examples.en: Her research centers on soil quality.
examples.cn: 她的研究集中在土壤质量上。

dict_mnemonic.text: center 里有 cent：把一百样东西摆匀，正中间那一点就是中心。

root: 源自希腊语 kentron（尖点、圆规定点），经拉丁语 centrum 与古法语 centre 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The compass point gives the geometric middle, a gathering place gives the institutional sense, and the verb makes something that middle.
sensesIntro.cn: 圆规定点给出几何中心，聚集之地给出机构义，动词则让某物成为那个中心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the fixed point of a compass, equally distant from every edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：圆规的定点，与每条边都等距。

branches.en: Geometry keeps the exact middle of a circle or room.
branches.cn: 几何义保留圆或房间的精确中点。

branches.en: A building where one activity gathers becomes its centre.
branches.cn: 某项活动聚集的建筑成为它的中心。

branches.en: The verb makes a topic or object the fixed point.
branches.cn: 动词义让话题或物件成为定点。

branches.en: Both senses involve one place that everything else is measured from.
branches.cn: 两个义项都涉及一个用来衡量其他一切的地点。

branches.en: Both senses share the idea of concentrating attention in one spot.
branches.cn: 两个义项都共享把注意力集中到一处之意。

intro.en: Center forms -al, -ally and -ist derivatives and keeps a British spelling with -re.
intro.cn: center 构成 -al、-ally、-ist 派生词，并有 -re 的英式拼写。

latinIntro.en: Latin centrum is the bridge from Greek kentron to the modern English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 centrum 是从希腊语 kentron 到现代英语词的桥梁。

items.example: The center is marked in red.
The city has three sports centers.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市有三个体育中心。

items.example: He centered the picture on the wall.

items.meaning: the act of placing in the middle
items.example: Centering the text took a moment.
items.exampleCN: 把文字居中花了一会儿。

items.meaning: in the middle or most important

items.exampleCN: 这套公寓位于中心地段。
中间派候选人赢得了席位。

latinEntries.example: Centrum passed into French as centre.
latinEntries.exampleCN: centrum 传入法语成为 centre。

definition_zh: 票价；费
definition_en: the money paid for a journey, or to get on in a particular way
core_image: 公交车门口，乘客刷卡付费后走向座位
scene: 他刷卡付了公交车费。 He paid the bus fare with a card.
sceneCN: 这里 fare 是「车费」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他刷卡支付了公交车费。

senses.title: Travel price
senses.definition: the money a passenger pays for a journey
senses.definitionCN: 乘客为一段行程支付的钱
senses.example: The train fare has gone up again.
senses.exampleCN: 火车票价又涨了。
senses.why: The core sense is the price of being carried.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是被运送所需支付的价格。

senses.title: Cost of food or service
senses.definition: the cost of meals, entertainment, or a service
senses.definitionCN: 餐食、娱乐或服务的费用
senses.example: The hotel offers simple local fare.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒店提供简单的当地饭菜。
senses.why: Travel costs extend to the cost of food along the way.
senses.whyCN: 旅途开销扩展为途中饮食的费用。

senses.title: Get on in life
senses.definition: to experience good or bad fortune in a situation
senses.definitionCN: 在某情境中经历好运或坏运
senses.example: The team fared well in the competition.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍在比赛中表现出色。
senses.why: How a journey goes becomes how life goes.
senses.whyCN: 旅程如何变成生活如何。

intro.en: Fare comes from Old English faran, to journey, and faru, a journey.
intro.cn: fare 源自古英语 faran（旅行）与 faru（旅程）。

items.en: Faran meant to travel.
items.cn: faran 意为旅行。

items.en: Faran meant to go or journey; faru meant a journey.
items.cn: faran 意为行走、旅行；faru 意为旅程。

items.en: Fare named the cost of a journey.
items.cn: fare 指旅程的费用。

items.en: Fare extended to food provided for a journey.
items.cn: fare 扩展到旅途中提供的食物。

items.en: Fare means a ticket price or how someone gets on.
items.cn: 现代英语中 fare 指票价或某人的境遇。

note.en: Fare is compared with homophones and with words for prices.
note.cn: 把 fare 与同音词以及表示价格的词作比较。

entries.definition: just and equal
entries.definitionCN: 公平的

entries.definition: at a great distance
entries.definitionCN: 远

entries.definition: the feeling of danger
entries.definitionCN: 恐惧

entries.definition: the money needed to buy something
entries.definitionCN: 价格

entries.definition: the money asked for a service
entries.definitionCN: 收费

entries.definition: money paid for a service
entries.definitionCN: 费用

normalIntro.en: Fare and fair sound the same but one is money and one is justice.
normalIntro.cn: fare 与 fair 同音，但一个指钱，一个指公平。

normal.en: Fare is what you pay to travel.
normal.cn: fare 是你出行要付的钱。

normal.en: Fair is justice; fare is money, so keep the e.
normal.cn: fair 是公平，fare 是钱，注意 fare 有 e。

normal.en: Fare well means get on well.
normal.cn: fare well 意为进展顺利。

normal.en: Bus fare and train fare are everyday phrases.
normal.cn: bus fare 和 train fare 是日常搭配。

normal.en: Fare as food appears in local fare and simple fare.
normal.cn: fare 指食物时见于 local fare 与 simple fare。

abstract.en: A fare is the price of moving from one place to another.
abstract.cn: 票价是从一处到另一处的代价。

abstract.en: How you fare is how your journey through events goes.
abstract.cn: 你 fare 得如何，就是你在事件旅程中走得如何。

abstract.en: One word covers travel cost, food, and fortune.
abstract.cn: 一个词涵盖旅费、食物与命运。

examples.en: How much is the fare to the airport?
examples.cn: 到机场的票价是多少？

examples.en: The children pay half fare.
examples.cn: 孩子们付半价。

examples.en: The small restaurant serves simple fare.
examples.cn: 这家小餐馆供应简单的饭菜。

dict_mnemonic.text: fare 与 fair 同音；fair 是「公平」，fare 是「出行要付的钱」，也可指旅途中的饭菜与境遇。

root: 源自古英语 faran（旅行）与 faru（旅程），核心义「一段旅程所需的代价与经历」。

sensesIntro.en: Fare means the price of a journey, the cost of food or service, or how someone gets on.
sensesIntro.cn: fare 意为旅费、餐食或服务费用，或某人的境遇进展。

core.en: The cost and experience of a journey.
core.cn: 一段旅程的代价与经历。

branches.en: The price paid for transport.
branches.cn: 为交通支付的价钱。

branches.en: The cost of meals and service.
branches.cn: 餐食与服务费用。

branches.en: How a person or team gets on.
branches.cn: 人或团队的进展境遇。

branches.en: Travel and food both cost money.
branches.cn: 出行与饮食都要花钱。

branches.en: A journey and a life both have a fare.
branches.cn: 旅程与人生都有其「代价与走向」。

intro.en: Fare forms compounds about tickets and travel.
intro.cn: fare 构成关于票务与旅行的复合词。

latinIntro.en: Fare is Germanic, so no Latin root is listed.
latinIntro.cn: fare 属日耳曼语，因此不列拉丁词根。

items.meaning: a travel price or to get on

items.example: They fared badly in the storm.
items.exampleCN: 他们在风暴中境况不佳。

items.meaning: a card used to pay fares
a person who travels on foot

definition_zh: 奢侈；奢华；奢侈品；难得的享受；豪华的
definition_en: great comfort and expensive pleasure, a costly thing that is not necessary, a rare pleasure one allows oneself, or used before a noun for goods and places that are costly and high-grade
core_image: 橱窗里一只镶着金边的手袋，灯光把它照得像有温度
scene: 老城区的橱窗里摆着一只镶着金边的手袋，标价牌被灯光照得发亮。 The shop window was filled with luxury goods that few people walking past could afford.
sceneCN: 这里 luxury 是「奢侈品」（第 2 个义项：并非必需而价格高昂的东西）；句意为橱窗里摆满了很少有人在路过时买得起的奢侈品。图中可辨识物件：老城区橱窗、镶金边的手袋、标价牌。

pos.zh: 奢侈；奢华；奢侈品；难得的享受

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁词干 luxuri- 加 -ous 构成，义为「奢华的；豪华的」
由 luxurious 加 -ly 构成，义为「奢华地」
与 luxury 同一拉丁词干，义为「茂盛的；丰富的」，偏指生长繁密而非昂贵

senses.title: Great comfort and costly pleasure
senses.definition: a style of life full of expensive comfort and pleasure, more than plain need requires
senses.definitionCN: 充满昂贵舒适与享乐的生活方式，远超朴素的需要
senses.example: They lived in luxury after the business took off.
senses.exampleCN: 生意兴隆之后，他们过上了奢华的生活。
senses.why: Latin luxuria named excess and rank growth; the modern sense keeps that image of something spilling past the limit of what is needed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 luxuria 本指过度与繁茂的生长；现代义保留了「漫过所需限度」这一意象。

senses.title: A costly thing that is not necessary
senses.definition: an expensive object or service bought for pleasure rather than for need
senses.definitionCN: 为享乐而非为需要购买的昂贵物品或服务
senses.example: The watch is a luxury, not a necessity.
senses.exampleCN: 这块表是奢侈品，不是必需品。
senses.why: Once excess becomes a style of life, its objects can be counted one by one, so the abstract quality turns into things a person can own.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「过度」成为一种生活方式，它的物件就能一件件数出来，于是抽象的性质变成了可以拥有的具体东西。

senses.title: A rare pleasure one allows oneself
senses.titleCN: 难得的享受；小小的奢侈
senses.definition: something pleasant and not essential that a person allows themselves only now and then
senses.definitionCN: 令人愉快却并非必需、只偶尔允许自己享受的事物
senses.example: A long bath at the end of the week is a luxury.
senses.exampleCN: 周末结束时泡个长澡，是一种难得的享受。
senses.why: The word can shrink from a whole way of life to a single small indulgence, because the pleasure still costs more than ordinary routine would allow.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以从一整种生活方式缩小为一次小小的放纵，因为这份愉悦仍然比日常惯例所允许的更费钱费力。

senses.title: Costly and high-grade, before a noun
senses.definition: used before a noun for goods, travel or housing that are expensive and meant to feel superior
senses.definitionCN: 用于名词之前，指昂贵且刻意营造高级感的商品、旅行或住宅
senses.example: They booked a luxury suite for the anniversary.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为纪念日订了一间豪华套房。
senses.why: English often turns a noun of excess into a label placed before another noun, so the thing being sold carries the promise of the whole category.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把表示过度的名词变成放在另一名词前的标签，于是被出售的东西就带上了整个类别的承诺。

intro.en: Luxury comes from Latin luxus and luxuria, words for excess and profusion, which passed through Old French luxurie before English used it for costly comfort.
intro.cn: luxury 来自拉丁语 luxus 与 luxuria，意为过度与繁盛；它经古法语 luxurie 进入英语，后来才指昂贵的舒适。

items.en: Luxus names excess, extravagance and lavish display; a second Latin sense, a dislocation or displacement, is sometimes linked to it, but the relation between the two is debated.
items.cn: luxus 指过度、奢靡与铺张的展示；拉丁语中它另有一个「错位、脱节」的义项，有人把两者联系起来，但二者关系仍有争论。

items.en: Luxuria, built on luxus, means excess and profusion, and it also describes the rank, over-lush growth of plants.
items.cn: 由 luxus 构成的 luxuria 意为过度与繁盛，也用来描述植物疯长、过于茂密的生长。

items.en: Old French luxurie carries the word into English with a moral tone, meaning lust and dissolute living.
items.cn: 古法语 luxurie 带着道德评判把这词带进英语，意为淫欲与放荡的生活。

items.en: In Middle English luxurie is first a vice of excess, and only later does it drift towards costly comfort.
items.cn: 在中古英语里，luxurie 起初是一种过度放纵的恶习，后来才慢慢转向昂贵的舒适。

items.en: By the eighteenth century luxury has lost much of its moral sting, and in the twentieth century it also works as an adjective before nouns such as hotel and suite.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，luxury 的道德锋芒已大大减弱；到二十世纪，它还能作形容词放在 hotel、suite 这类名词之前。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the Latin-stem family of adjectives and adverbs; the near-meaning group gathers words for wealth, excess and comfort.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词干上的形容词与副词；近义组收表示财富、过度与舒适的词。

entries.definition: Very comfortable and costly, as a room, a car or a life.
entries.definitionCN: 同一拉丁词干构成的形容词，义为「奢华的；豪华的」。

entries.definition: In a costly and comfortable manner.
entries.definitionCN: 由 luxurious 加 -ly 构成，义为「奢华地」。

entries.definition: Growing thickly and richly, used of hair, plants or style.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词干的形容词，义为「茂盛的；丰富的」，偏指生长繁密。

entries.definition: The quality of growing thickly or being richly abundant.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词干的名词，义为「繁茂；丰盛」。

entries.definition: Great wealth shown openly in costly things and surroundings.
entries.definitionCN: 富裕；强调公开显示的财富与排场，比 luxury 更偏炫耀。

entries.definition: Spending more than is reasonable or necessary.
entries.definitionCN: 铺张；强调花费超出合理或必需，带批评色彩。

entries.definition: A pleasant state of ease without effort or pain.
entries.definitionCN: 舒适；只强调身心的安逸，不含昂贵之意。

entries.definition: Impressive and expensive beauty, especially of a place.
entries.definitionCN: 辉煌；强调视觉上的华美与气派，多用于场所。

normalIntro.en: The word goes back to Latin nouns for excess, and its family keeps returning to lavishness, growth beyond bounds and costly comfort.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词上溯到表示过度的拉丁名词，同族词反复回到奢靡、越界生长与昂贵的舒适。

normal.en: Luxury goes back to Latin luxus, excess, so the word still carries the idea of more than need requires.
normal.cn: luxury 上溯到拉丁语 luxus（过度），所以这个词仍带着「超出所需」的意思。

normal.en: Latin luxuria also named the rank growth of plants, so lavishness and a plant spilling past its bounds share one picture.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 luxuria 也指植物疯长，所以铺张与植物漫出边界共享同一幅画面。

normal.en: Luxurious, luxuriant and luxury share one stem, but luxurious describes costly comfort while luxuriant describes thick growth.
normal.cn: luxurious、luxuriant 与 luxury 共用一个词干，但 luxurious 指昂贵的舒适，luxuriant 指茂密的生长。

normal.en: The French form luxurie came into English with a moral sting, meaning dissolute living before it meant fine things.
normal.cn: 法语形式 luxurie 带着道德批评进入英语，先指放荡的生活，后来才指精美的东西。

normal.en: In the lap of luxury is the fixed phrase for a life surrounded by costly comfort.
normal.cn: in the lap of luxury 是形容生活被昂贵舒适包围的固定说法。

abstract.en: A word born from excess suggests that luxury is defined not by objects but by the line they cross.
abstract.cn: 一个从「过度」中诞生的词说明，奢侈不由物品定义，而由它越过的界线定义。

abstract.en: The same root grows plants and sells suites, which is why richness always looks like something spilling over its edges.
abstract.cn: 同一个词根既让植物疯长，也用来卖套房，所以「丰盛」总像某种漫出边缘的东西。

abstract.en: Luxury is what comfort becomes when it stops answering a need and starts answering a desire.
abstract.cn: 奢侈就是舒适不再回应需要、转而回应欲望时的样子。

examples.en: The shop window was filled with luxury goods that few people walking past could afford.
examples.cn: 橱窗里摆满了很少有人在路过时买得起的奢侈品。

examples.en: They lived in luxury after the business took off.
examples.cn: 生意兴隆之后，他们过上了奢华的生活。

examples.en: They booked a luxury suite for the anniversary.
examples.cn: 他们为纪念日订了一间豪华套房。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「乐奢瑞」——日子过得乐、又舍得奢，才叫 luxury；记住它是奢侈、奢华。

root: 拉丁语 luxus（过度、奢靡）与 luxuria（过量、繁茂的生长）经古法语 luxurie 进入英语；一般认为核心是「超出限度」，luxus 两义之间的关系学界仍有争论；luxurious、luxuriant 都从这一词干而来。

sensesIntro.en: The core is excess beyond need; the senses divide into a lavish way of life, costly objects, a small rare indulgence, and the adjective for high-grade goods.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是超出所需的过度；义项由此分出奢华的生活方式、昂贵的物件、偶尔的小小放纵，以及指高级商品的形容词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gold-trimmed handbag in a shop window, lit until it seems warm.
core.cn: 核心意象：橱窗里一只镶着金边的手袋，灯光把它照得像有温度。

branches.en: a house kept far larger than the family needs
branches.cn: 一所远超家庭所需的房子

branches.en: a gold-trimmed bag behind lit glass
branches.cn: 灯光玻璃柜后镶金边的手袋

branches.en: a long bath taken without hurry
branches.cn: 不慌不忙泡的一个长澡

branches.en: a hotel door held open by a doorman
branches.cn: 门童替你拉开的酒店大门

branches.en: a price tag turned towards the light
branches.cn: 被转向灯光的标价牌

intro.en: The word is a Latin stem of excess with a French ending; its family adds the suffixes -ous and -ly to build the adjective and the adverb.
intro.cn: 这个词是表示过度的拉丁词干加上法语词尾；它的同族词加 -ous 与 -ly 构成形容词与副词。

latinIntro.en: Luxury has a recorded Latin family: luxus, luxuria and luxuriosus all belong to the same stem of excess and profusion.
latinIntro.cn: luxury 有可靠的拉丁同族词：luxus、luxuria 与 luxuriosus 都属于表示过度与繁盛的同一词干。

items.meaning: costly comfort or a costly thing
items.exampleCN: 这间套房是纯粹的奢华。

items.meaningCN: 构成表示「充满……」的形容词后缀

items.example: They stayed in a luxurious hotel.
items.exampleCN: 他们住进一家豪华酒店。

items.example: The garden was luxuriant after the rains.

definition_zh: 驯服的；温顺的；乏味的；驯服
definition_en: not wild and willing to live with people, dull, or to make an animal gentle
core_image: 野马低下头让人系上缰绳
scene: 老人花了整个夏天才驯服那匹野马。 The old man spent the whole summer taming the wild horse.
sceneCN: 这里 tame 是「驯服」（第 3 个义项）；句意：老人花了整个夏天才驯服那匹野马。

senses.title: Not wild
senses.definition: used to living with people and not dangerous
senses.definitionCN: 已经习惯与人相处、没有野性的
senses.example: The once wild bird is now tame.
senses.exampleCN: 那只曾经野性的鸟现在很温顺。
senses.why: The oldest sense is an animal brought into the household.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是被带进家门的动物。

senses.title: Dull and unexciting
senses.definition: not exciting or interesting
senses.definitionCN: 不刺激、不有趣的
senses.example: The film had a tame ending.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影的结局很平淡。
senses.why: A tame animal is safe, and safe easily slides into dull.
senses.whyCN: 驯服的动物意味着安全，而安全很容易滑向「乏味」。

senses.title: To make an animal gentle
senses.definition: to train a wild animal to live with people
senses.definitionCN: 训练野生动物与人共处
senses.example: The old man spent the whole summer taming the wild horse.
senses.exampleCN: 老人花了整个夏天才驯服那匹野马。
senses.why: The adjective turned into the work of making something tame.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转化为「使某物变温顺」的工作。

intro.en: Tame is an old Germanic word for animals brought into the home.
intro.cn: tame 是古老的日耳曼词，指被带进家中的动物。

items.en: The root meant tame or domestic.
items.cn: 词根意为驯服的、家养的。

items.en: Tam meant gentle and domesticated.
items.cn: tam 意为温顺、家养的。

items.en: Tame kept the animal sense.
items.cn: tame 保留了动物义。

items.en: Tame extended to dull and unexciting.
items.cn: tame 扩展到「乏味」的含义。

items.en: The verb means to make gentle.
items.cn: 动词义为使之温顺。

note.en: Tame is compared with look-alike words and with words for gentle animals.
note.cn: 把 tame 与形近词以及表示温顺的词作对比。

entries.definition: not different
entries.definitionCN: 相同的；只拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: one who tames animals
entries.definitionCN: 驯兽师

entries.definition: in a gentle way
entries.definitionCN: 温顺地

entries.definition: kept by people
entries.definitionCN: 家养的

entries.definition: calm and not rough
entries.definitionCN: 温顺的

entries.definition: not interesting
entries.definitionCN: 乏味的

normalIntro.en: Tame describes the moment a wild creature accepts a human hand.
normalIntro.cn: tame 描述野兽接受人手的那一刻。

normal.en: The old man spent the summer taming the horse.
normal.cn: 老人花了一个夏天驯服那匹马。

normal.en: The rabbit grew tame and ate from her hand.
normal.cn: 兔子变得温顺，从她手里吃东西。

normal.en: The story has a rather tame ending.
normal.cn: 这个故事结局相当平淡。

normal.en: Farm animals are tame by nature.
normal.cn: 农场动物天性温顺。

normal.en: She works as a lion tamer.
normal.cn: 她是一名驯狮师。

abstract.en: Wildness is trained into trust.
abstract.cn: 野性被训练成信任。

abstract.en: Safe can turn dull if nothing surprises us.
abstract.cn: 若没有惊喜，安全也会变得乏味。

abstract.en: A tamed river still carries its force.
abstract.cn: 被治理的河流仍带着力量。

examples.en: The old man spent the whole summer taming the wild horse.
examples.cn: 老人花了整个夏天才驯服那匹野马。

examples.en: The once wild bird is now tame.
examples.cn: 那只曾经野性的鸟现在很温顺。

examples.en: The film had a tame ending.
examples.cn: 这部电影的结局很平淡。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「太木」——野兽被驯得「太木」了，连脾气都没了，就是 tame。

root: 古英语 tam（温顺、家养），源自日耳曼语，与德语 zahm 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Tame starts with domestic animals, slides into dullness, and becomes the act of taming.
sensesIntro.cn: tame 从家养动物出发，滑向「乏味」，又变成驯服的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wild head bowing to a human hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：野性的头低下来靠近人手。

branches.en: Domestication is the original sense.
branches.cn: 家养是最初的义项。

branches.en: Safety without surprise feels dull.
branches.cn: 没有惊喜的安全显得乏味。

branches.en: The verb is the work of taming.
branches.cn: 动词指驯服这件事。

branches.en: Adjective and verb describe one process.
branches.cn: 形容词与动词描述同一个过程。

branches.en: Both remove danger and excitement.
branches.cn: 两者都移除了危险与刺激。

intro.en: Tame builds a small family through -er, -ly, and -ness.
intro.cn: tame 通过 -er、-ly、-ness 构成小词族。

latinIntro.en: Tame is Germanic; Latin domare, to tame, is its semantic cousin.
latinIntro.cn: tame 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 domare（驯服）是它的语义对应词。

definition_zh: 宝石；珠宝；珍贵的人或物
definition_en: a precious stone cut and polished for ornament, or something highly valued
core_image: 一束光照进切割好的宝石，里面折出一片细小的彩虹
scene: 老钟表匠把放大镜戴上，从盒子里取出一粒小小的蓝石头嵌进表盘。 The crown is set with three jewels.
sceneCN: 这里 jewel 是「宝石」（第 1 个义项：经切割打磨的贵重石料），句意为王冠上镶着三颗宝石。画面里的物件：放大镜、蓝石头、表盘。

pos.zh: 名词：宝石；珠宝；珍贵之物

collocations.zh: 王冠上的明珠；最珍贵的部分

derivatives.zh: 由本词词干加 -lery 构成，义为「珠宝首饰」
由本词加 -ler 构成，义为「珠宝商」
由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「镶有宝石的」
美式拼写的同族词，义为「珠宝」

senses.title: A cut gemstone
senses.definition: a rare stone cut and polished to be worn as ornament
senses.definitionCN: 经切割与打磨、可佩戴作饰的稀有石料
senses.example: The ring holds a single jewel the size of a pea.
senses.exampleCN: 这枚戒指上嵌着一颗豌豆大小的宝石。
senses.why: The stone sense is the base; everything else in the word grows from it.
senses.whyCN: 石头义是根底，这个词的其余用法都从它长出来。

senses.title: Jewellery as a whole
senses.definition: ornaments set with such stones, often kept as family property
senses.definitionCN: 镶有此类石料的饰物，常被当作家产保管
senses.example: The jewels were hidden under the floor for thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这些珠宝在地板下面藏了三十年。
senses.why: In the plural the word shifts from one stone to the whole collection.
senses.whyCN: 用复数时，词义从单颗石头转到整批首饰。

senses.title: Something precious
senses.definition: a person or thing that is greatly valued for its quality
senses.definitionCN: 因品质而被人极为看重的人或物
senses.example: The little library is the jewel of the town.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小图书馆是镇上的宝贝。
senses.why: The metaphor is generous: any great thing can be called a jewel.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻很宽容：任何出色的东西都能叫 jewel。

intro.en: Jewel reached English through Old French, and its deeper root is debated: game or grace are the usual candidates.
intro.cn: jewel 经由古法语进入英语，更深的词根有争议，常见说法是「玩物」或「恩典」。

items.en: A late Latin word jocale meant "plaything", from jocus, "joke".
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 jocale 意为「玩物」，来自 jocus「玩笑」。

items.en: French turned it into jouel, "a precious ornament".
items.cn: 法语把它变成 jouel「贵重饰物」。

items.en: Anglo-Norman carried the word into English records.
items.cn: 盎格鲁-诺曼语把这个词带入英语文献。

items.en: Middle English wrote it as juel or jewell.
items.cn: 中古英语写作 juel 或 jewell。

items.en: The spelling settled on jewel, and the "precision" metaphor grew.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 jewel，随后又长出「珍贵之物」的比喻。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the j- and -el outline; the near-meaning group holds words for precious things.
note.cn: 形近组共用 j- 与 -el 的外形；近义组收表示珍品的词。

entries.definition: The American spelling for ornaments.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「珠宝」，美式拼写。

entries.definition: A person who sells jewels.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「珠宝商」，同族词。

entries.definition: Decorated with gems.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「镶宝石的」，同族词。

entries.definition: A precious stone, especially cut.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「宝石」，最常用近义词。

entries.definition: A hard round body formed inside an oyster.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「珍珠」，来自贝壳。

entries.definition: Valuable objects or something deeply valued.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「珍宝」，范围更广。

normalIntro.en: These hooks link the stone to the plaything it once meant.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把宝石连到它早先「玩物」的意思上。

normal.en: Late Latin jocale meant a plaything.
normal.cn: 晚期拉丁语 jocale 意为玩物。

normal.en: A thing of play turned into a thing of price.
normal.cn: 玩物变成了有价钱的东西。

normal.en: One stone is a jewel; many are jewellery.
normal.cn: 一颗叫 jewel，一串叫 jewellery。

normal.en: The seller of them is a jeweller.
normal.cn: 卖它的人叫 jeweller。

normal.en: Anything lovely enough gets called a jewel.
normal.cn: 任何足够可爱的东西都能被叫作 jewel。

abstract.en: Jewels are light trained to stay in one place.
abstract.cn: 宝石是被训练得停在一处的光。

abstract.en: Value is cut into a stone by patience.
abstract.cn: 价值是被耐心一道一道切进石头里的。

abstract.en: A good librarian is a jewel nobody puts in a case.
abstract.cn: 好馆员是不进匣子的宝石。

examples.en: The jeweller set the stone in a thin gold band.
examples.cn: 珠宝商把宝石镶在细金环上。

examples.en: She wore no jewels, only her mother's watch.
examples.cn: 她没戴珠宝，只戴着母亲的手表。

examples.en: The old bridge is the jewel of the river walk.
examples.cn: 这座老桥是沿河步道上最珍贵的一段。

dict_mnemonic.text: jewel 由 jouel 而来，本是「玩物」，后来成了宝石

root: 晚期拉丁语 jocale「玩物」← jocus「玩笑」→ 古法语 jouel「贵重饰物」→ 盎格鲁-诺曼语 → 中古英语 juel → 现代英语 jewel。同族有 jewellery、jeweller、jeweled。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: a single cut stone, ornaments as a collection, and anything highly valued.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：单颗切割宝石、成串的珠宝首饰，以及任何极受珍视之物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: light folded inside a cut stone into a small rainbow.
core.cn: 核心意象：光在切割好的石头里折成一道小彩虹。

branches.en: THE STONE: one cut gem waiting for a setting.
branches.cn: 石头这条线：一颗等着镶座的刻面宝石。

branches.en: THE CASE: a family box of ornaments.
branches.cn: 首饰盒这条线：一只装家传饰物的匣子。

branches.en: THE PRAISE: a place or person worth more than money.
branches.cn: 赞誉这条线：比钱更值的地方或人。

branches.en: THE HAND: both senses pass from hand to hand.
branches.cn: 手这条线：两个义项都靠人与人相传。

branches.en: THE KEEPING: what is precious gets locked away and pointed at.
branches.cn: 珍藏这条线：珍品既被锁起，也被指给人看。

intro.en: Jewel is borrowed whole from French; the added endings are the learnable parts.
intro.cn: jewel 是从法语整体借来的，只有后面加的词尾是能拆的部分。

latinIntro.en: Latin jocale sits behind the French word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 jocale 是法语词的前身。

items.example: It marks the word as a little object.
It forms jewelled, set with gems.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 jewelled，镶有宝石的。

items.example: The root points to play, not wealth.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指的是玩，不是财富。

definition_zh: 保护的；防护的；保护性的
definition_en: giving protection from harm, damage or loss
core_image: 一双厚手套把易碎的玻璃杯包住，杯壁不再直接受力
scene: 野外摄影师在镜头前又加了一层薄膜。 A thin protective coating keeps the lens from scratching in the field.
sceneCN: 这里 protective 指「起防护作用、使对象免受损伤」（第 1 个义项：在物体表面加一层屏障以抵挡磨损）；句意为野外加的一层薄防护膜使镜片不被刮伤。图中可辨识物件：镜头、透明薄膜、沙砾、相机包；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 保护的；防护的；保护性的

senses.title: Shielding an object from damage
senses.definition: forming a barrier that keeps an object from being scratched, worn or broken
senses.definitionCN: 形成屏障，使物件不被刮伤、磨损或打破
senses.example: A thin protective coating keeps the lens from scratching in the field.
senses.exampleCN: 一层薄防护膜使镜片在野外不被刮伤。
senses.why: -ive marks function: the coating exists in order to protect, whether or not it is currently doing so.
senses.whyCN: -ive 标记功能：这层膜的存在目的就是保护，不论此刻是否正在受力。

senses.title: Careful in guarding people
senses.definition: used of a person who watches over others so closely that it limits their freedom
senses.definitionCN: 形容一个人过度看护他人，以至限制对方自由
senses.example: His protective manner kept his younger brother from making friends.
senses.exampleCN: 他那过度保护的态度让弟弟交不到朋友。
senses.why: Care can become a barrier, so the same adjective covers a parent's vigilance.
senses.whyCN: 照料可以变成屏障，因此同一个形容词也覆盖家长的警觉。

senses.title: Legal measure that keeps someone safe
senses.definition: a court order or legal status that shields a person from harm or harassment
senses.definitionCN: 使某人免受伤害或骚扰的法院命令或法律地位
senses.example: The court issued a protective order after the threat.
senses.exampleCN: 在威胁发生之后，法院发布了保护令。
senses.why: A court order is a legal coating around a person.
senses.whyCN: 法院命令是裹在人身上的一层法律涂层。

senses.title: Coloration that hides or warns
senses.titleCN: 起隐藏或警告作用的体色
senses.definition: used of colours that help an animal avoid detection or advertise a defence
senses.definitionCN: 形容帮助动物避免被发现或通告防御手段的颜色
senses.example: Protective coloration makes the nestlings nearly invisible.
senses.exampleCN: 保护色让雏鸟几乎看不见。
senses.why: Colour is the animal's own coating, grown instead of worn.
senses.whyCN: 体色是动物自带的涂层，长出来而非穿上去。

senses.title: Tariff that shields local industry
senses.definition: used of a tax on imports intended to raise the price of foreign competitors
senses.definitionCN: 形容旨在提高外国竞争者价格的进口税
senses.example: The protective tariff kept the mill open for another decade.
senses.exampleCN: 保护性关税让这家工厂又开了十年。
senses.why: A tariff is a wall placed around a domestic market.
senses.whyCN: 关税是围在国内市场外的一道墙。

senses.title: Custody for a person's safety
senses.definition: used of detention intended to keep a person from harm rather than to punish
senses.definitionCN: 形容旨在使某人免受伤害而非惩罚的拘留
senses.example: The witness was held in protective custody overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 那名证人被以保护性拘留关押了一夜。
senses.why: Custody keeps a person inside a legal shield.
senses.whyCN: 拘留把一个人留在法律盾牌之内。

senses.title: Factor that reduces risk
senses.definition: used of a condition or habit that lowers the chance of a bad outcome
senses.definitionCN: 形容降低不良结果几率的条件或习惯
senses.example: Regular sleep is a protective factor for adolescent mental health.
senses.exampleCN: 规律睡眠是青少年心理健康的保护因素。
senses.why: A habit acts before the harm, which is what a protective layer does.
senses.whyCN: 习惯在伤害之前起作用，这正是防护层的作用。

senses.title: Instinct to guard the young
senses.definition: used of an animal's instinctive readiness to defend its offspring
senses.definitionCN: 形容动物保护后代的本能反应
senses.example: The mother bear's protective instinct made the trail impassable.
senses.exampleCN: 母熊的护幼本能让那条小路无法通行。
senses.why: The instinct puts the parent's body between the danger and the young.
senses.whyCN: 本能把亲本的身体放在危险与幼体之间。

intro.en: Protective comes from protect, from Latin protegere 'to cover in front', built on pro- 'before' and tegere 'to cover'. The adjective protectivus is late Latin; English protective appears in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: protective 来自 protect，后者出自拉丁 protegere「在前面遮盖」，由 pro-「在前」与 tegere「覆盖」构成。形容词 protectivus 为晚期拉丁；英语 protective 于 16 世纪出现。

items.en: Tegere 'to cover' supplies the core image of a roof or shield placed over something.
items.cn: tegere「覆盖」提供核心意象：把屋顶或盾牌置于某物之上。

items.en: Protegere joined pro- 'in front' to tegere, giving 'to cover in front, to shield'.
items.cn: protegere 把 pro-「在前」与 tegere 结合，意为「在前面遮盖、屏蔽」。

items.en: The noun protectio 'a covering, protection' supplied the action noun behind protect and protection.
items.cn: 名词 protectio「遮盖、保护」提供了 protect 与 protection 背后的动作名词。

items.en: French protectif carried the adjective into English, where protective is recorded from the 1500s.
items.cn: 法语 protectif 把这个形容词带入英语，protective 自 16 世纪有记录。

items.en: Protective tariff and protective custody are eighteenth- and nineteenth-century specializations.
items.cn: 保护性关税与保护性拘留是 18、19 世纪的特化用法。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact first English use of protective is unrecorded and the sixteenth-century date is approximate. The Latin protegere and tegere layers are secure.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：protective 的最早英语使用无记录，16 世纪之数为约数；拉丁 protegere 与 tegere 这两层可靠。

note.en: Group one separates the adjective from the verb, noun and adverb of the family; group two separates kinds of shielding by purpose.
note.cn: 第一组区分该形容词与同族动词、名词、副词；第二组按目的区分各类屏蔽。

entries.definition: The state or act of being protected; protective describes what provides it.
entries.definitionCN: 指被保护的状态或行为；protective 描述提供保护的事物。

entries.definition: A person or device that protects; protective is a quality, not an agent.
entries.definitionCN: 指起保护作用的人或装置；protective 是性质，不是施动者。

entries.definition: In a protecting manner; it modifies a verb rather than describing a thing.
entries.definitionCN: 指以保护的方式；修饰动词，而非描述事物。

entries.definition: The tendency to protect; the adjective describes, the noun names the trait.
entries.definitionCN: 指保护倾向；形容词描述，名词命名特质。

entries.definition: Oriented against an attack; protective need not imply any attacker.
entries.definitionCN: 指针对攻击的取向；protective 不一定暗示攻击者。

entries.definition: Acting before harm occurs; protective describes the barrier, preventive the timing.
entries.definitionCN: 指在伤害发生前行动；protective 描述屏障，preventive 描述时机。

entries.definition: Providing cover or refuge; protective is broader and includes coatings and laws.
entries.definitionCN: 指提供遮蔽或庇护；protective 更宽，包含涂层与法律。

entries.definition: The ongoing activity of keeping someone safe; protective is the quality of the measure.
entries.definitionCN: 指持续使某人安全的行动；protective 是措施的性质。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real pro- plus tegere structure, the real family, and the fixed phrases for clothing, law, trade and health.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的 pro- 加 tegere 结构、真实词族，以及衣物、法律、贸易与健康领域的固定搭配。

normal.en: pro- 'in front' + tegere 'cover' + -ive: tending to cover in front.
normal.cn: pro-「在前」+ tegere「覆盖」+ -ive：倾向于在前面遮盖。

normal.en: The family runs protect, protection, protective, protector, protectively.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 protect、protection、protective、protector、protectively。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: protective clothing, protective coating, protective order.
normal.cn: 固定搭配有 protective clothing、protective coating、protective order。

normal.en: The same adjective serves gloves, laws, tariffs and instincts.
normal.cn: 同一个形容词可用于手套、法律、关税与本能。

normal.en: Compare protection, the noun, and protector, the agent.
normal.cn: 比较名词 protection 与施动者 protector。

abstract.en: Picture thick gloves closed around a glass that must not break.
abstract.cn: 想象厚手套包住一只绝不能破的玻璃杯。

abstract.en: Picture a transparent film taking every scratch that the lens would have taken.
abstract.cn: 想象一层透明膜替镜片承受了每一道刮痕。

abstract.en: Picture a parent standing one step too close to a child's every decision.
abstract.cn: 想象一位家长站得离孩子的每个决定都太近。

examples.en: Workers wore protective masks around the solvent.
examples.cn: 工人在溶剂旁戴着防护口罩。

examples.en: The law provides protective measures for witnesses.
examples.cn: 法律为证人提供保护措施。

examples.en: Protective coloration kept the eggs hidden from above.
examples.cn: 保护色使这些卵从上方看不被发现。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「protect（保护）+ -ive（性质）」——带着保护性质的 → 防护的；保护性的

root: 拉丁 pro-「在前」+ tegere「覆盖」→ protegere「在前面遮盖」→ 晚期拉丁 protectivus → 法语 protectif → 英语 protective。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one covering: a film over a lens, a parent over a child, a court over a witness, colour over a nest, a tariff over a mill, custody over a witness, a habit over health, and an instinct over cubs.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一层覆盖：薄膜覆镜片、家长护孩子、法院护证人、体色护巢、关税护工厂、拘留护证人、习惯护健康、本能护幼崽。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: thick gloves closed around a fragile glass, taking the force instead of it.
core.cn: 核心意象：厚手套包住易碎玻璃，替它承受力量。

chain: THE LAYER IS MADE A RULE

branches.en: PHYSICAL COVER: coatings and body colour absorb damage or hide the young.
branches.cn: 物理覆盖：涂层与体色吸收损伤或藏住幼体。

branches.en: CARE: a person or animal stands between danger and the one guarded.
branches.cn: 看护：人或动物站危险与被护者之间。

branches.en: LAW: orders and custody replace the body with legal walls.
branches.cn: 法律：命令与拘留用法律墙壁替代身体。

branches.en: TRADE: a tariff is a wall around a domestic industry.
branches.cn: 贸易：关税是围住本国产业的一道墙。

branches.en: HEALTH: a habit lowers risk before harm appears.
branches.cn: 健康：习惯在伤害出现前降低风险。

intro.en: Protective is a Latin verb stem plus -ive; the Latin family of protegere supplies the verb, the action noun and the agent.
intro.cn: protective 是拉丁动词词干加 -ive；protegere 的拉丁词族提供动词、动作名词与施动者。

latinIntro.en: Latin protegere, protectio and tectus supply the idea of covering something in front.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 protegere、protectio 与 tectus 提供「在前面覆盖某物」的意思。

items.example: The wall protects the village from wind.
items.exampleCN: 这堵墙保护村庄免受风。

items.example: Protection from rain was the first concern.
The coating is protective, not decorative.
items.exampleCN: 这层涂层是防护性的，不是装饰性的。

items.example: A surge protector guards the equipment.

items.exampleCN: 他的过度保护成了负担。

items.example: Protective clothing is required near acid.
items.exampleCN: 在酸附近必须穿防护服。

items.example: The protective tariff raised import prices.
items.exampleCN: 保护性关税抬高了进口价格。

items.example: The child was placed in protective custody.
items.exampleCN: 那名儿童被置于保护性拘留。

definition_zh: 皇帝；君主；帝王
definition_en: the male sovereign ruler of an empire; a monarch with this title; a dominant figure in a field
core_image: 高座上的人一抬手，整片疆域都跟着动
scene: 宫殿大门缓缓打开，群臣向高座行礼。 The emperor received the envoys in the great hall.
sceneCN: 这里 emperor 是「皇帝」（第 01 个义项：帝国的男性最高统治者）；句意是皇帝在大殿接见使节。

derivatives.zh: 由同一词族演变而来的阴性形式，义为「女皇；皇后」
由本词加 -ship 构成，义为「皇位；皇帝身份」
由本词与 penguin 复合，义为「帝企鹅」

senses.title: The ruler of an empire
senses.definition: the male sovereign who rules an empire
senses.definitionCN: 统治一个帝国的男性君主
senses.example: The emperor received the envoys in the great hall.
senses.exampleCN: 皇帝在大殿接见使节。
senses.why: The Latin source is a commander who gives orders, so the emperor is the one whose command holds an empire together.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源头是发号施令的统帅，所以皇帝就是那个用命令把帝国维系在一起的人。

senses.title: A monarch with this title
senses.definition: a king or sovereign who formally holds the title of emperor
senses.definitionCN: 正式拥有皇帝称号的国王或君主
senses.example: The emperor of Japan has a largely ceremonial role.
senses.exampleCN: 日本天皇的角色主要是礼仪性的。
senses.why: A title can outlive the power behind it, so emperor also names a rank that may now be ceremonial.
senses.whyCN: 称号可以比它背后的权力活得更久，所以 emperor 也指一种如今可能只剩礼仪意义的位号。

senses.title: A dominant figure in a field
senses.definition: a person who dominates a particular activity or industry
senses.definitionCN: 在某一活动或行业中占据统治地位的人
senses.example: He was called the emperor of modern retail.
senses.exampleCN: 他被称为现代零售业的皇帝。
senses.why: One who rules a territory and one who rules a market share the image of command, so the title extends to industry leaders.
senses.whyCN: 统治疆域的人与统治市场份额的人共享「发号施令」的画面，于是这个称号扩展到行业领袖身上。

intro.en: Emperor goes back to Latin imperator, a commander, and to the verb imperare, to command.
intro.cn: emperor 可追溯到拉丁语 imperator（统帅）与动词 imperare（命令）。

items.en: Parare meant to prepare or order.
items.cn: parare 意为准备、安排。

items.en: With in-, the verb meant to command or give orders.
items.cn: 加上 in- 后，动词意为命令、发号施令。

items.en: Imperator named a commander, later a victorious general hailed by troops.
items.cn: imperator 指统帅，后来指被军队拥立的胜利将领。

items.en: Empereor carried the title into French.
items.cn: empereor 把这个称号带入法语。

items.en: English emperor now names the ruler of an empire and, figuratively, a dominant leader.
items.cn: 现代英语 emperor 既指帝国统治者，也比喻某一领域的霸主。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the imperial family; the near-meaning group separates king, monarch and ruler.
note.cn: 形近组沿着帝国词族展开；近义组区分国王、君主与统治者。

entries.definition: The territory or domain that an emperor rules.
entries.definitionCN: 同根词，义为「帝国」，即皇帝统治的疆域。

entries.definition: A female emperor or the wife of an emperor.
entries.definitionCN: 同词族，义为「女皇；皇后」。

entries.definition: Relating to an empire or an emperor.
entries.definitionCN: 同根词，义为「帝国的；皇帝的」。

entries.definition: The male ruler of a kingdom, usually below an emperor in rank.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「国王」，级别通常低于皇帝。

entries.definition: A general word for a king, queen or emperor.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「君主」，是国王、女王、皇帝的统称。

entries.definition: Anyone who governs a country or people.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「统治者」，范围最宽。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie emperor to command and to empire, then let the title reach a ceremonial throne and an industry leader.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把 emperor 与「命令」「帝国」绑在一起，再让这个称号走到礼仪王座与行业领袖。

normal.en: Imperare means to command, and the emperor commands.
normal.cn: imperare 意为命令，皇帝就是发号施令的人。

normal.en: An emperor rules an empire.
normal.cn: 皇帝统治帝国。

normal.en: The emperor penguin borrows the title for its size.
normal.cn: 帝企鹅借这个称号来形容体型。

normal.en: An empress is the female counterpart.
normal.cn: empress 是女性对应形式。

normal.en: An industry emperor rules a market instead of a country.
normal.cn: 行业皇帝统治的是市场而不是国家。

abstract.en: Picture a single raised hand that moves a whole map.
abstract.cn: 想象一只抬起的手，牵动整张地图。

abstract.en: The word is command given a throne.
abstract.cn: 这个词就是「命令」被安上了一张王座。

abstract.en: Old titles can survive after the power has gone.
abstract.cn: 旧称号可以在权力消失后继续活着。

examples.en: The emperor received the envoys in the great hall.
examples.cn: 皇帝在大殿接见使节。

examples.en: The emperor of Japan has a largely ceremonial role.
examples.cn: 日本天皇的角色主要是礼仪性的。

examples.en: He was called the emperor of modern retail.
examples.cn: 他被称为现代零售业的皇帝。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「恩婆热」——全城的人都得听他一人的

root: 经古法语 empereor 来自拉丁语 imperator（统帅），其动词 imperare 由 in-（向内、在上）加 parare（安排、命令）构成。

sensesIntro.en: Emperor is the commander who rules an empire, then a formal title, then a dominant figure in any field.
sensesIntro.cn: emperor 先是统治帝国的统帅，再是一种正式称号，最后指任何领域中的霸主。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a raised hand on a throne moving a whole territory.
core.cn: 核心意象：王座上一只抬起的手，牵动整片疆域。

branches.en: THE RULER: the sovereign of a whole empire.
branches.cn: 统治者线：整个帝国的君主。

branches.en: THE TITLE: a rank that may outlive real power.
branches.cn: 称号线：可能比实权活得更久的位号。

branches.en: THE TYCOON: a market ruled like a country.
branches.cn: 巨头线：像统治国家一样统治市场。

branches.en: POWER AND FORM: the ruler and the formal rank.
branches.cn: 权力与形式：统治者与正式位号。

branches.en: LAND AND MARKET: two territories under one word.
branches.cn: 疆域与市场：同一个词下有两片领地。

intro.en: Emperor is a French borrowing from Latin imperator, so its endings are historical rather than productive.
intro.cn: emperor 是经法语借入的拉丁语词，其词尾属于历史沉积而非能产词缀。

latinIntro.en: Imperare, imperator and imperium are recorded Latin forms of command and authority.
latinIntro.cn: imperare、imperator 与 imperium 都是有记录的拉丁语形式，表示命令与权威。

items.example: It is the base of imperare.
It gives the ruler his power.

definition_zh: 醋；尖刻；坏脾气
definition_en: a sour liquid made from wine or cider and used in cooking, or a sour temper
core_image: 一勺深褐色的液体倒进凉菜，酸味冲上来
scene: 厨房里，她把醋倒进拌好的黄瓜，酸味立刻充满了屋子。 A spoonful of vinegar gives the salad its sharp taste.
sceneCN: 这里 vinegar 是「醋」（第 1 个义项：由葡萄酒或苹果酒发酵成的酸味液体，用于调味）；句意为一勺醋让沙拉有了锐利的酸味。倒进凉菜时窜上来的酸味正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 加后缀 -y 构成，义为「酸的；尖刻的」
加后缀 -ish 构成，义为「略带酸味的」
加 -oon 构成的旧词，义为「醋虫；鞭蝎」

senses.title: A sour liquid used in cooking
senses.definition: a sour liquid produced by fermenting wine, cider, or malt, used to flavour food
senses.definitionCN: 由葡萄酒、苹果酒或麦芽发酵而成、用于调味的酸味液体
senses.example: A spoonful of vinegar gives the salad its sharp taste.
senses.exampleCN: 一勺醋让沙拉有了锐利的酸味。
senses.why: Old French vyn egre means sour wine, and sour wine is exactly what vinegar is.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 vyn egre 意为「酸酒」，而醋正是变酸的酒。

senses.title: A sour or sharp temper
senses.definition: a bitter or ill-tempered manner in speech or behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 言语或行为中尖刻、易怒的性情
senses.example: His reply was all vinegar and no help.
senses.exampleCN: 他的回答满是尖刻，毫无帮助。
senses.why: Taste words often become temper words: what stings the tongue also stings the ear.
senses.whyCN: 味道词常变成性情词：刺舌的东西也刺耳。

senses.title: In industry, a dilute acid
senses.definition: a dilute acetic acid used in cleaning, preserving, or manufacture
senses.definitionCN: 用于清洁、防腐或制造的稀醋酸
senses.example: The workshop cleans metal parts in vinegar before painting.
senses.exampleCN: 车间在喷漆前用稀醋酸清洗金属件。
senses.why: Beyond the kitchen, the same acid serves as a cheap and mild solvent.
senses.whyCN: 走出厨房，同一种酸也成了廉价温和的溶剂。

senses.title: A means of preserving food
senses.definition: a sour bath in which food is kept from spoiling
senses.definitionCN: 用来防止食物变坏的酸味浸泡液
senses.example: They keep onions in vinegar through the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用醋泡洋葱，能吃一冬天。
senses.why: The sourness that flavours food also protects it, so vinegar became a preservative.
senses.whyCN: 调味的酸同时能护住食物，于是醋成了防腐手段。

senses.title: A sharp, bitter remark
senses.definition: a comment that stings or embitters the hearer
senses.definitionCN: 刺痛或使听者不快的话
senses.example: Every suggestion was met with vinegar from the chair.
senses.exampleCN: 每个建议都被主席用尖刻的话顶了回去。
senses.why: When the temper shows itself in words, each remark is a drop of the same fluid.
senses.whyCN: 当脾气化作言语时，每一句话都是同一液体的液滴。

intro.en: Vinegar is French for sour wine: vin, wine, plus aigre, sour.
intro.cn: vinegar 就是法语的「酸酒」：vin（酒）加 aigre（酸）。

items.en: Vinum meant wine, and acer meant sharp or sour.
items.cn: vinum 意为酒，acer 意为尖的、酸的。

items.en: Vyn egre joined the two words into sour wine.
items.cn: vyn egre 把两个词合为一体，指酸酒。

items.en: English took it as vynegre in the kitchen and in medicine.
items.cn: 英语以 vynegre 借入，用于厨房和医药。

items.en: The spelling settled as vinegar in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 十七世纪拼写固定为 vinegar。

items.en: A sour temper and a sharp remark took the taste word out of the kitchen.
items.cn: 坏脾气与尖刻话把这个味觉词带出了厨房。

note.en: The first group holds the vinegar family, the second the sour tastes and sharp manners it stands beside.
note.cn: 第一组是 vinegar 词族，第二组是与酸味、尖刻并列的词。

entries.definition: sour, or sharp in manner
entries.definitionCN: 酸的；尖刻的

entries.definition: slightly sour
entries.definitionCN: 略带酸味的

entries.definition: the plant that bears grapes
entries.definitionCN: 葡萄藤

entries.definition: a common misspelling
entries.definitionCN: 常见错拼

entries.definition: a sour chemical substance
entries.definitionCN: 酸

entries.definition: a sour citrus fruit
entries.definitionCN: 柠檬

entries.definition: having a sharp taste
entries.definitionCN: 酸的

entries.definition: resentment in the heart
entries.definitionCN: 怨恨；苦涩

normalIntro.en: Wine that has turned sour: that is the whole word, and the whole bottle.
normalIntro.cn: 变酸的酒——这就是整个词，也是整瓶东西。

normal.en: Vinegar hides vin, wine, at the front.
normal.cn: vinegar 前头藏着 vin，即葡萄酒。

normal.en: The -ar at the end echoes aigre, sour in French.
normal.cn: 结尾的 -ar 呼应法语 aigre（酸的）。

normal.en: Vinegar has three syllables: VIN-e-gar.
normal.cn: vinegar 有三个音节：VIN-e-gar。

normal.en: Add -y for vinegary, sour or sharp.
normal.cn: 加 -y 得 vinegary，酸的或尖刻的。

normal.en: Do not confuse vinegar with vine, the grape plant.
normal.cn: 别把 vinegar 与 vine（葡萄藤）混为一谈。

abstract.en: See dark liquid tipping from a spoon into a bowl.
abstract.cn: 想深色液体从勺里倒进碗里。

abstract.en: Smell sharp air rising from a salad.
abstract.cn: 嗅沙拉上窜起的冲鼻气。

abstract.en: Hear a voice turn sour at the end of a sentence.
abstract.cn: 听一句话的尾音突然变酸。

examples.en: Mix olive oil and vinegar for the dressing.
examples.cn: 把橄榄油和醋调成沙拉汁。

examples.en: A drop of vinegar cuts the sweetness of the sauce.
examples.cn: 一滴醋能压住酱汁的甜腻。

examples.en: There was vinegar in every word she said.
examples.cn: 她说的话里每一句都带刺。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂泥哥」——喂，泥哥，快闻闻这瓶醋，酸得呛人。

root: 拉丁语 vinum（酒）+ acer（酸的）→ 古法语 vyn egre（酸酒）→ 英语 vinegar

sensesIntro.en: Sour wine in a bottle becomes a seasoning, a preservative, an industrial acid, and at last a sour temper.
sensesIntro.cn: 瓶里的酸酒先成为调味品、防腐液、工业稀酸，最后成为酸溜溜的脾气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: dark vinegar dripping onto a salad.
core.cn: 核心意象：深色的醋滴在沙拉上。

branches.en: The kitchen branch: a spoonful on cucumber.
branches.cn: 厨房分支：黄瓜上的一勺醋。

branches.en: The temper branch: a reply all vinegar.
branches.cn: 脾气分支：满是尖刻的回答。

branches.en: The workshop branch: acid for cleaning metal.
branches.cn: 车间分支：清洗金属的稀酸。

branches.en: The jar branch: onions kept through winter.
branches.cn: 坛子分支：醋泡洋葱过冬。

branches.en: The remark branch: every suggestion stung.
branches.cn: 言语分支：每个建议都被刺回。

intro.en: Vinegar came into English whole from French; only -y and -ish were added later.
intro.cn: vinegar 从法语整体进入英语，后来只加上了 -y 与 -ish。

latinIntro.en: Its parts are Latin vinum, wine, and acer, sharp, joined in Old French before English borrowed it.
latinIntro.cn: 其成分是拉丁语 vinum（酒）与 acer（尖的），在古法语中先已拼合，英语整体借用。

items.exampleCN: vinegar 中的 vin- 意为酒。

items.example: A vinegarish smell filled the room.
items.exampleCN: 屋里有一股微酸的气味。

items.example: Vine and vinegar look close but differ.
items.exampleCN: vine 与 vinegar 形近而义远。
wine 与 vinegar 同出 vinum。

items.example: Write vinegar with an e after v.
items.exampleCN: vinegar 在 v 后写 e。

items.example: Sour describes what vinegar tastes of.

definition_zh: 授予；赋予；商议；协商
definition_en: to give an honour or right to someone, or to discuss something with others
core_image: 校长把一枚奖章别在学生胸前
scene: 校长在典礼上把奖学金证书交给那位学生。 The school will confer an award on her at the ceremony.
sceneCN: 这里 confer 指「授予」（第 1 个义项：把荣誉或权利正式给予某人）；句意是学校将在典礼上授予她一个奖项。

senses.title: Give an honour or right
senses.definition: to officially give someone an honour, degree or right
senses.definitionCN: 正式把荣誉、学位或权利给予某人
senses.example: The university conferred a degree on him.
senses.exampleCN: 大学授予他一个学位。
senses.why: A gift of status must be given in public to count.
senses.whyCN: 身份的赠予必须在公开场合给出才算数。

senses.title: Talk something over
senses.definition: to discuss a matter with other people before deciding
senses.definitionCN: 在做决定前与他人讨论某事
senses.example: The judges conferred quietly before they voted.
senses.exampleCN: 评委在投票前低声商议。
senses.why: Two heads brought together can see more than one.
senses.whyCN: 两个脑袋凑在一起，能看到一个人看不到的东西。

intro.en: Confer comes from Latin conferre, to bring together, built from com-, together, and ferre, to carry.
intro.cn: confer 来自拉丁语 conferre，意为带到一起，由 com-（一起）与 ferre（携带）构成。

items.en: Ferre meant to carry or bring something to a place.
items.cn: ferre 意为把某物携带或带到某处。

items.en: Conferre meant to bring things or people into one place.
items.cn: conferre 意为把东西或人带到同一个地方。

items.en: It also came to mean to compare, since comparing brings two things side by side.
items.cn: 它也引申为比较，因为比较就是把两样东西并排放到一起。

items.en: English confer first meant to compare and then to consult.
items.cn: 英语 confer 最初表示比较，随后表示商议。

items.en: It now also means to give an honour or a right in a formal way.
items.cn: 如今它也指以正式方式授予荣誉或权利。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that rhyme with confer, and the meaning group names other ways of giving or discussing.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 confer 押韵的词，近义组列出其他表示给予或商议的说法。

entries.definition: to mention or send someone for help
entries.definitionCN: 提到；转介

entries.definition: to put something off to a later time
entries.definitionCN: 推迟；延缓

entries.definition: to reach a conclusion from evidence
entries.definitionCN: 推断；推论

entries.definition: to give something formally or legally
entries.definitionCN: 授予；准予

entries.definition: to give an honour as a gift
entries.definitionCN: 授予；赠予

entries.definition: to ask someone for advice or information
entries.definitionCN: 咨询；商议

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a medal on a stage, then move to a small circle of judges and to a gift of rights.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从台上的奖章开始，再走到围坐的评委与一份权利的赠予。

normal.en: Con- is together and fer- is carry, so confer is to carry something to someone.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，fer- 是携带，所以 confer 就是把东西送到别人那里。

normal.en: A degree conferred is a paper carried across a stage.
normal.cn: 被授予的学位，就是一张被带上台的纸。

normal.en: Judges confer because a decision carried by several minds weighs more.
normal.cn: 评委要商议，因为几个人共同作出的决定更有分量。

normal.en: Confer with a friend before you confer a promise.
normal.cn: 在给出承诺之前，先和朋友商议一下。

normal.en: The same word gives an honour and asks for advice.
normal.cn: 同一个词，既给出荣誉，也征求建议。

abstract.en: Picture a medal laid in an open hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚奖章被放进摊开的手掌。

abstract.en: Picture three chairs pulled into a tight circle.
abstract.cn: 想象三把椅子被拉成一个紧圈。

abstract.en: Picture two maps laid side by side on a table.
abstract.cn: 想象两张地图并排摊在桌上。

examples.en: The college conferred an honorary degree on her.
examples.cn: 学院授予她荣誉学位。

examples.en: The doctors conferred before they began the operation.
examples.cn: 医生们在手术开始前进行了商议。

examples.en: You should confer with your family first.
examples.cn: 你应该先和家人商量。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 confer 记成 con（一起）加 fer（带）：把荣誉带给人是授予，把问题带到一起讨论就是商议。

root: 源自拉丁语 conferre（com 一起 + ferre 携带），本义是带到一起，后引申为比较、商议与授予。

sensesIntro.en: From carrying things into one place, to talking a matter over, and finally to handing an honour to someone.
sensesIntro.cn: 从把东西带到一处，到把事情放在一起讨论，最后到把荣誉交到某人手上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people bring their views to one table, and one brings a gift to the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个人把看法带到同一张桌上，同时一个人把礼物递给另一个人。

branches.en: An honour is carried from the giver to the receiver.
branches.cn: 荣誉从授予者手中被送到接受者那里。

branches.en: A discussion brings several minds into one place.
branches.cn: 商议把几个人的想法带到同一个地方。

branches.en: Both senses depend on bringing people or things together.
branches.cn: 两个义项都依赖把人或事物带到一起。

branches.en: The act of conferring is the short meeting before a decision.
branches.cn: 商议就是做决定前的那场短会。

branches.en: The giving sense carries the same image into ceremony.
branches.cn: 授予义项把同一个意象带进了典礼。

intro.en: Confer is built on Latin com-, together, plus ferre, to carry.
intro.cn: confer 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 ferre（携带）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin carry base fer- also appears in transfer, refer and offer.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的携带词基 fer- 也出现在 transfer、refer 与 offer 中。

items.exampleCN: 这个头衔带来很大的尊重。

items.example: They are conferring in the next room.
items.exampleCN: 他们正在隔壁房间商议。

items.meaning: the act of giving an honour
items.exampleCN: 这次授予在安静中完成。

items.meaning: the giving of a degree or right
items.example: The conferral of the prize was delayed.
They transferred the file to a new drive.
items.exampleCN: 他们把文件转到了新硬盘上。

definition_zh: 肢；四肢；大树枝；延伸部分；孤立无援的处境
definition_en: an arm, leg or wing; a large branch of a tree; and a risky or unsupported position, chiefly in the phrase out on a limb
core_image: 橡树粗壮的横枝朝一侧伸出，像一条展开的手臂
scene: 台风过后，院子里那棵老橡树被劈掉一大截横枝，断口露出浅色的木芯。 The storm tore a heavy limb from the oak and left it lying across the path.
sceneCN: 这里是「大树枝」（第 2 个义项：从树干分出的大枝）；句意为暴风把橡树的一根粗枝劈下，横在路面上。图中可辨识物件：断枝、浅色木芯、湿漉的院子。

pos.zh: 肢；四肢；大树枝；延伸部分；孤立无援的处境

derivatives.zh: 由 limb 加 -ed 构成，义为「有……肢的」，多用于复合形容词
由 limb 加否定后缀 -less 构成，义为「无肢的」
由 long 与 limbed 复合而成，义为「四肢修长的」

senses.title: An arm, leg or wing
senses.definition: a leg, arm or wing of a person or animal, especially one of the paired parts used for movement
senses.definitionCN: 人或动物的腿、臂或翼，尤指成对用于活动的部分
senses.example: He stretched his aching limbs after the long walk.
senses.exampleCN: 长途步行之后，他伸展酸痛的四肢。
senses.why: Old English lim named a jointed part of the body, and the word keeps that bodily core before it extends to other branching things.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 lim 指身体上有关节的部分，这个词先守住身体这一核心，再扩展到别的「分出的部分」。

senses.title: A large branch of a tree
senses.definition: a large branch growing out from the trunk of a tree
senses.definitionCN: 从树干长出的粗大枝条
senses.example: The storm tore a heavy limb from the oak.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风把橡树的一根粗枝劈了下来。
senses.why: A branch leaves the trunk the way a limb leaves the body, so a word for a projecting part of a body was applied to a projecting part of a tree.
senses.whyCN: 树枝从树干分出，正如肢体从身体长出，于是这个指「身体外伸部分」的词也用到了树上。

senses.title: A vulnerable or isolated position
senses.titleCN: 孤立无援的处境；危险的境地
senses.definition: used in the phrase out on a limb to mean in a risky or unsupported position
senses.definitionCN: 用于 out on a limb 这一短语，表示身处危险或无人支持的境地
senses.example: By speaking first, she put herself out on a limb.
senses.exampleCN: 她第一个发言，把自己置于孤立无援的境地。
senses.why: A limb is what holds you up; to be out on one is to stand on a narrow branch far from the trunk, with nothing to hold on to.
senses.whyCN: 肢体本来是支撑身体的东西；而 out on a limb 就是跑到远离树干的窄枝上，身边没有可扶持的东西。

intro.en: Limb is an old Germanic word for a body part, and part of its history remains uncertain.
intro.cn: limb 是一个古老的日耳曼语词，指身体的一部分，它的历史有一部分并不清楚。

items.en: A form reconstructed as limu- is thought to have meant limb, but its links to other roots remain uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为有一个重构形式 limu-，意为「肢体」，但它与其他词根的联系仍不确定。

items.en: Old English lim meant a limb or a jointed part of the body, and it could already be used of a branch.
items.cn: 古英语 lim 指肢体或身体上有关节的部分，而且已经可以用来指树枝。

items.en: Middle English wrote lim and limbe; the final b was added in spelling, probably by association with other words rather than by a change in sound.
items.cn: 中古英语写作 lim 与 limbe；词尾的 b 是拼写上添上去的，可能与别的词发生了联想，而不是读音变化。

items.en: Sixteenth-century printers fixed the spelling limb, and the b stayed even though it is never pronounced.
items.cn: 十六世纪的印刷者把拼写固定为 limb，这个 b 从不发音却被保留下来。

items.en: Modern English extends limb to tree branches, to the arms and legs of anatomy, and to the phrase out on a limb.
items.cn: 现代英语把 limb 扩展到树枝、解剖学上的四肢，以及 out on a limb 这一短语。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on limb and a few close spellings; the near-meaning group collects the parts it can name.
note.cn: 形近组收由 limb 构成的词形和几个拼写相近的词；近义组收它可以指称的那些部位。

entries.definition: Having limbs of a stated kind, as in long-limbed.
entries.definitionCN: 有某种肢体的，如长肢的。

entries.definition: Without limbs of any kind.
entries.definitionCN: 没有任何肢体的。

entries.definition: A place of waiting or neglect; the spelling is close, but the word comes from Latin limbus, meaning a border, so the two are not related.
entries.definitionCN: 等待或被人遗忘的境地；拼写相近，但这个词来自拉丁语 limbus（边界），两者不同源。

entries.definition: Supple and able to bend easily; its origin is uncertain and any link with limb is only suggested by the spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 柔软、容易弯曲的；来源不确定，与 limb 的联系只是拼写上的暗示。

entries.definition: The upper limb from the shoulder to the hand.
entries.definitionCN: 从肩到手的上肢。

entries.definition: The lower limb used for standing and walking.
entries.definitionCN: 用于站立和行走的下肢。

entries.definition: A part growing out from the trunk of a tree.
entries.definitionCN: 从树干长出的部分。

entries.definition: A large branch of a tree, chiefly in literary use.
entries.definitionCN: 树的大枝，多见于文学语言。

normalIntro.en: The word is short and old, so its hooks come from the body, the tree and the idiom it feeds.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词短而古老，所以记忆钩子来自身体、树木，以及它养出的那个习语。

normal.en: Old English lim meant a jointed body part, so the first picture is an arm or a leg, not a branch.
normal.cn: 古英语 lim 指有关节的身体部分，所以第一幅画面是手臂或腿，而不是树枝。

normal.en: The b in limb is silent and was added by printers; pronounce the word as lim and the spelling makes sense.
normal.cn: limb 里的 b 不发音，是印刷者添上去的；按 lim 来读，拼写就说得通。

normal.en: A branch is a limb of a tree because it leaves the trunk as an arm leaves the shoulder.
normal.cn: 树枝是树的 limb，因为它离开树干的方式，正如手臂离开肩膀。

normal.en: Out on a limb pictures someone standing on a narrow branch, far from any support.
normal.cn: out on a limb 画出一个人站在窄枝上，远离任何支撑。

normal.en: Limbed and limbless are built with -ed and -less, so they describe what a body or a doll has or lacks.
normal.cn: limbed 与 limbless 分别由 -ed、-less 构成，用来描述身体或人偶有或者没有肢体。

abstract.en: The body's branches and the tree's branches share one word because both reach out from a centre.
abstract.cn: 身体的分支与树的分支共用一个词，因为两者都从一个中心向外伸。

abstract.en: A limb is both a support and an exposure: what lets you stand can also leave you stranded.
abstract.cn: 肢体既是支撑也是暴露：让你站稳的东西，也能让你困在险处。

abstract.en: A silent letter is a small reminder that spelling often records the accidents of printers rather than the history of sound.
abstract.cn: 一个不发音的字母提醒人：拼写记下的常是印刷者的偶然选择，而不是声音的历史。

examples.en: He stretched his aching limbs after the long walk.
examples.cn: 长途步行之后，他伸展酸痛的四肢。

examples.en: The storm tore a heavy limb from the oak.
examples.cn: 暴风把橡树的一根粗枝劈了下来。

examples.en: She put herself out on a limb by speaking first.
examples.cn: 她第一个发言，把自己置于孤立无援的境地。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「林木」——林木伸出的大枝像一条手臂；limb 是肢体，也是大树枝。

root: 古英语 lim（肢体；身体有关节的部分），一般认为源自重构形式 limu-（肢体），与其他词根的联系不确定；词尾 b 为拼写添加；拉丁语 limbus（边界）只是形近，并非同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a part that reaches out from a main body; the senses divide into the limbs of a body, the branches of a tree, and the risky position of standing on a narrow branch.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「从主体伸出的部分」；义项由此分为身体肢体、树木大枝，以及站在窄枝上的危险处境。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick oak branch reaching out to one side like an opened arm.
core.cn: 核心意象：橡树粗壮的横枝朝一侧伸出，像一条展开的手臂。

branches.en: a swimmer stretching both arms
branches.cn: 游泳者伸开的双臂

branches.en: a broken bough across a path
branches.cn: 横在路上的断枝

branches.en: a voice speaking alone in a meeting
branches.cn: 会上独自开口的声音

branches.en: a shape reaching out from a centre
branches.cn: 从一个中心伸出的形状

branches.en: a figure standing on a thin branch
branches.cn: 站在细枝上的身影

intro.en: The word has no prefix, so the entries are its Germanic ancestors, its English forms and the suffixes it takes.
intro.cn: 这个词没有前缀，因此条目是它的日耳曼语先祖、英语词形，以及它接受的几个后缀。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 蚊子；蚊虫滋扰；蚊媒疾病的传播者；蚊的幼虫（作定语）；蚊帐等防蚊用品（作定语）；小型舰艇编队（蚊队）；蚊叮的小伤；被当作猎物的小飞虫（如蚊鹰）
definition_en: a small two-winged fly whose female bites and sucks blood, often carrying disease; also used of the nuisance, the diseases it spreads and small craft fleets
core_image: 水面上倒立着一只细腿小虫，口器像一根细针，背后是静止的池水与一圈涟漪
scene: 池塘边，一只蚊子把细长的口器刺进人的前臂。 A mosquito pierces the skin of a sleeper's forearm with its needle-like mouthparts.
sceneCN: 这里 mosquito 指「吸血的小型双翅目昆虫」（第 1 个义项：蚊）；句意为一只蚊子用针状口器刺入睡者前臂的皮肤。可辨识物件：细长口器、透明翅膀、前臂、池水；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: A small blood-sucking fly
senses.titleCN: 蚊子：吸血的小型双翅目昆虫
senses.definition: a small two-winged fly whose female pierces skin and takes blood
senses.definitionCN: 雌虫刺穿皮肤吸血的细小双翅目昆虫
senses.example: A mosquito pierces the skin of a sleeper's forearm with its needle-like mouthparts.
senses.exampleCN: 一只蚊子用针状口器刺入睡者前臂的皮肤。
senses.why: Only the female bites, because she needs blood protein for her eggs; the everyday word still names the whole insect.
senses.whyCN: 只有雌虫叮咬，因为它需要血液中的蛋白质来产卵；日常用词仍指整个虫体。

senses.title: A biting nuisance
senses.definition: mosquitoes treated collectively as an irritating swarm that drives people indoors
senses.definitionCN: 把蚊虫看成一群扰人的飞虫，能把人赶进屋里
senses.example: The mosquitoes drove the whole camp indoors before dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 蚊群还没到黄昏就把整个营地的人赶进了屋。
senses.why: When the plural is used this way, the word names an annoyance rather than a species.
senses.whyCN: 复数这样用时，词指的是扰人的麻烦，而不是某个物种。

senses.title: A disease vector
senses.definition: the insect understood as the carrier that passes malaria, dengue or other infections between people
senses.definitionCN: 被理解为在人与人之间传递疟疾、登革热等感染的媒介昆虫
senses.example: Mosquitoes carry malaria in lowland regions.
senses.exampleCN: 蚊子在低地地区传播疟疾。
senses.why: Public health shifted the emphasis from the bite to the transmission chain, and this sense now dominates medical writing.
senses.whyCN: 公共卫生把重点从叮咬转到传播链，这一义如今在医学写作中占主导。

senses.title: The aquatic young stage
senses.definition: the larval form that hangs at the water surface, usually named in the compound mosquito larva
senses.definitionCN: 倒悬在水面的幼虫，通常以「mosquito larva」这一复合形式出现
senses.example: Mosquito larvae hang head-down just beneath the surface film.
senses.exampleCN: 孑孓头朝下挂在表面水膜之下。
senses.why: The adult name is reused as a modifier for its own young, a common pattern in entomology.
senses.whyCN: 成虫名被复用作自身幼期的修饰语，这是昆虫学中常见的模式。

senses.title: Protective gear against mosquitoes
senses.definition: the equipment named after the insect, such as a mosquito net, coil or repellent
senses.definitionCN: 以这种昆虫命名的防护用品，如蚊帐、蚊香或驱蚊剂
senses.example: A mosquito net over the bed is the cheapest protection.
senses.exampleCN: 床上挂一顶蚊帐是最便宜的防护。
senses.why: The word marks what the object is used against, so the insect name becomes a label for the defence.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标出物件用来对付什么，昆虫名于是成了防护手段的标签。

senses.title: A fleet of small craft
senses.definition: a group of tiny, fast boats or warships, historically called a mosquito fleet
senses.definitionCN: 一群小而快的船或军舰，历史上称作蚊队
senses.example: A mosquito fleet of wooden gunboats patrolled the river.
senses.exampleCN: 一支由木制炮艇组成的蚊队巡弋河面。
senses.why: The metaphor compares small, numerous, stinging craft to a swarm of biting insects.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把数量多、体量小、能刺痛人的舰艇比作一群叮人的虫。

senses.title: A small irritating wound
senses.definition: the itchy swelling left by a bite, commonly called a mosquito bite
senses.definitionCN: 叮咬留下的发痒肿块，通常说成「mosquito bite」
senses.example: A mosquito bite on his ankle kept him awake.
senses.exampleCN: 脚踝上的蚊叮让他一夜没睡好。
senses.why: Metonymy moves the name from the biter to the mark it leaves, a very common shift in medical everyday speech.
senses.whyCN: 转喻把名字从叮咬者移到留下的痕迹，这是医学口语中极常见的转移。

senses.title: A tiny flying prey
senses.titleCN: 被当作猎物的小飞虫（如蚊鹰）
senses.definition: a small flying insect understood as food for a predator, as in the folk name mosquito hawk
senses.definitionCN: 被看作捕食者食物的小飞虫，如俗称蚊鹰的蜻蜓
senses.example: Children call the dragonfly a mosquito hawk because it catches small flies.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们把蜻蜓叫作蚊鹰，因为它捕食小飞虫。
senses.why: Here mosquito names the prey, and the compound tells what the larger insect feeds on.
senses.whyCN: 此处 mosquito 指猎物，复合词说明那种更大的昆虫吃什么。

intro.en: Mosquito is a Spanish and Portuguese diminutive of mosca 'fly', from Latin musca. English borrowed it in the sixteenth century during exploration of the Americas.
intro.cn: mosquito 是西班牙语与葡萄牙语中 mosca「苍蝇」的指小形式，源自拉丁 musca。英语在 16 世纪探索美洲期间把它借入。

items.en: Latin musca meant 'fly'; its own deeper origin is not settled, and the Indo-European forms sometimes cited for it are reconstructions.
items.cn: 拉丁 musca 意为「苍蝇」；它更深的来源并无定论，偶尔为其引用的印欧形式属重构。

items.en: Spanish and Portuguese added the diminutive suffix -ito to mosca, giving mosquito 'little fly', the form English borrowed.
items.cn: 西班牙语与葡萄牙语给 mosca 加上指小后缀 -ito，构成 mosquito「小苍蝇」，英语借的就是这一形式。

items.en: English recorded mosquito in the late sixteenth century in travel accounts of the Caribbean and South America.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪后期的加勒比与南美游记中记录了 mosquito。

items.en: After the discovery that the insect transmits malaria and yellow fever, the word moved into public health vocabulary in the late nineteenth century.
items.cn: 在发现这种昆虫传播疟疾与黄热病之后，这个词于 19 世纪后期进入公共卫生词汇。

items.en: Both mosquitoes and mosquitos are accepted plurals; the longer form follows the older English habit of doubling the final consonant before -es.
items.cn: mosquitoes 与 mosquitos 两种复数都被接受；较长的一种沿用英语在 -es 前双写末尾辅音的老习惯。

items.en: Source uncertain (detail and first date): the deeper origin and the exact first citation are not settled, so any pre-Latin form offered here is a reconstruction and competing hypotheses are left side by side.
items.cn: 来源不确定（细节与首见年代）：更深的来源与确切最早书证均无定论，此处给出的拉丁语之前形式属重构形式，并列假说一并保留、不作定论。

note.en: Group one collects words that look or sound close but come from other roots; group two collects the small biting flies people mix up with mosquitoes.
note.cn: 第一组收形近音近但来源不同的词；第二组收人们常与蚊子混淆的小型叮咬蝇类。

entries.definition: Mosque comes from Arabic masjid, a place of prostration; the resemblance to mosquito is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: mosque 来自阿拉伯语 masjid，意为叩拜之处；与 mosquito 的相似纯属偶然。

entries.definition: Miskito names a people and a coast of Central America and is spelled with a k; it is not the insect.
entries.definitionCN: Miskito 指中美洲的一个民族与一片海岸，拼写带 k，不是这种昆虫。

entries.definition: This plural is a spelling variant of mosquitoes, not a different word with a different meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 这个复数只是 mosquitoes 的拼写变体，并非意义不同的另一个词。

entries.definition: The compound names the bed net, so the insect word is working as a modifier rather than as the subject.
entries.definitionCN: 这个复合词指床上用的蚊帐，昆虫词在此作修饰语而非主语。

entries.definition: A gnat is a very small biting fly, often a midge; it bites but does not transmit malaria.
entries.definitionCN: gnat 指极小的叮咬蝇，常为蠓；会叮人但不传播疟疾。

entries.definition: A midge is a minute two-winged fly, some species of which bite in swarms near water.
entries.definitionCN: midge 是极小的双翅目蝇，有些种类在水边成群叮人。

entries.definition: Fly is the general name for the order, of which the mosquito is one family.
entries.definitionCN: fly 是这一目的通称，蚊子只是其中一科。

entries.definition: A flea is a wingless jumping insect that bites; it belongs to a different order entirely.
entries.definitionCN: flea 是无翅跳跃的叮咬昆虫，属于完全不同的目。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Spanish mosca 'fly' plus the diminutive -ito gives mosquito, literally 'little fly'.
normal.cn: 西班牙语 mosca「苍蝇」加指小后缀 -ito 构成 mosquito，字面就是「小苍蝇」。

normal.en: The family runs mosquito, mosquitoes, mosquitos, mosquitofish and mosquitocide.
normal.cn: 词族包括 mosquito、mosquitoes、mosquitos、mosquitofish 与 mosquitocide。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: mosquito net, mosquito coil, mosquito-borne disease.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：蚊帐、蚊香、蚊媒疾病。

normal.en: Only the female bites; males feed on nectar.
normal.cn: 只有雌虫叮咬，雄虫吸食花蜜。

normal.en: The larval stage is the wriggler that hangs at the water surface.
normal.cn: 幼虫期就是倒悬在水面的孑孓。

abstract.en: Picture a needle so fine that the sleeper never feels it enter.
abstract.cn: 想象一根细到睡者完全察觉不到的针。

abstract.en: Picture a whole village sleeping under white gauze, one net per bed.
abstract.cn: 想象整个村子睡在白纱之下，每张床一顶帐。

abstract.en: Picture a hundred small boats stinging a harbour like a swarm.
abstract.cn: 想象上百条小船像虫群一样刺痛一座港口。

examples.en: The mosquito net was treated with insecticide and hung over both beds.
examples.cn: 蚊帐经杀虫剂处理，挂在两张床的上方。

examples.en: Mosquitoes breeding in standing water made the drainage project urgent.
examples.cn: 蚊子在积水中繁殖，使排水工程变得紧迫。

examples.en: A mosquito bite on her wrist swelled into a hard red lump.
examples.cn: 她手腕上的蚊叮肿成了一个硬红的包。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「mosquito（莫斯基托）」——在池边「莫」名其妙被叮一口的小虫 → 蚊子

root: 西班牙语/葡萄牙语 mosquito「小苍蝇」= mosca「苍蝇」+ 指小后缀 -ito；mosca 源自拉丁 musca「苍蝇」。拉丁 musca 更早来源不确定，所引印欧形式属重构形式。与 mosque（阿拉伯语 masjid）无关。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from the biting insect, spread to the swarm, the disease chain, its water-borne young, the gear used against it, small warships, the mark it leaves and the prey it becomes.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从叮人的昆虫出发，扩展到虫群、疾病链、水中幼期、对付它的器物、小型舰艇、留下的包以及它作为猎物的一面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a needle-thin mouthpart breaking the skin while a gauze net hangs above the bed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根细如针的口器刺破皮肤，床的上方挂着纱帐。

branches.en: THE BITE: the insect and the itchy mark it leaves are two ends of one act.
branches.cn: 叮咬：昆虫与它留下的痒包是同一动作的两端。

branches.en: THE SWARM: the nuisance and the wriggling young both present the insect in numbers.
branches.cn: 虫群：扰人的成蚊与扭动的幼虫都以数量呈现这种昆虫。

branches.en: TRANSMISSION: the bite becomes a link in a chain between patients.
branches.cn: 传播：叮咬成为病人之间链条上的一环。

branches.en: DEFENCE AND METAPHOR: nets and coils answer the bite, and small fast boats borrow it.
branches.cn: 防护与比喻：蚊帐蚊香回应叮咬，小而快的船借用了它。

branches.en: THE PREY: the name finally marks a food item for a larger hunter.
branches.cn: 猎物：名字最后标出一种更大捕食者的食物。

intro.en: Mosquito is a Spanish diminutive built on a Latin root; its English derivatives are compounds, while the Latin family supplies the technical terms.
intro.cn: mosquito 是在拉丁词根上构成的西班牙语指小词；英语派生词多为复合，技术术语则来自拉丁词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin musca 'fly' gives muscid and musciform in zoology; the Spanish diminutive is the branch that produced the English noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 musca「苍蝇」在动物学中给出 muscid 与 musciform；产生英语名词的是西班牙语指小这一支。

items.example: A mosquito rests on the shaded wall.
items.exampleCN: 一只蚊子在背阴的墙上停歇。
凡有积水处蚊子就能繁殖。

items.meaning: a net hung over a bed
items.example: The mosquito net kept the room quiet at night.
items.exampleCN: 蚊帐让夜里屋里安静下来。

items.example: A mosquito coil smoked in the corner.

items.meaning: a substance that keeps the insect off
items.example: The mosquito repellent smelled of lemon grass.
items.exampleCN: 驱蚊剂有柠檬草的味道。

items.meaning: a small fish that eats larvae
items.example: Mosquitofish were introduced to clear the ponds.
items.exampleCN: 人们引入食蚊鱼来清理池塘。

items.meaning: a substance that kills the insect
items.example: The spray is a mosquitocide for drains.
items.exampleCN: 这种喷雾是用于排水沟的灭蚊剂。

items.example: A mosquito hawk hovered over the path.
items.exampleCN: 一只蚊鹰在小径上方悬停。

definition_zh: 指导；教授；指示；命令
definition_en: to teach someone how to do something, or to tell them officially what to do
core_image: 老师在黑板前把步骤一层层码好，学生在下面照着做
scene: 驾校场地上，教练扶着方向盘，让学员慢慢松离合。 The coach instructed the players to keep the ball low.
sceneCN: 这里 instruct 是「指示、吩咐」（第 2 个义项：正式告诉某人该做什么），句意是教练指示球队把球压低。画面里能看到的物件：方向盘、黑板、步骤清单。

pos.zh: 动词：指导；教授；指示；命令

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ion 构成，义为「指导；说明；指示」
由本词加 -or 构成，义为「教练；讲师」
由本词加 -ive 构成，义为「有教益的」

senses.title: To teach
senses.definition: to teach a person or a group a skill or subject, often in a formal setting
senses.definitionCN: 在正式场合中教授某人或某群体一项技能或科目
senses.example: She instructs new drivers on small roads first.
senses.exampleCN: 她先在小路上教新司机。
senses.why: Latin struere means to pile up or build; in- plus struere builds knowledge inside the learner.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 struere 意为「堆起、建造」；in- 加 struere 就是在学习者内心把知识搭起来。

senses.title: To give an order
senses.definition: to tell someone officially or firmly what they must do
senses.definitionCN: 正式或坚决地告诉某人必须做什么
senses.example: The judge instructed the jury to ignore the remark.
senses.exampleCN: 法官指示陪审团忽略那句话。
senses.why: Teaching and commanding share a structure: someone with knowledge stands above someone without it.
senses.whyCN: 教学与命令共享一个结构：有知识的人站在无知识的人之上。

senses.title: To employ someone professionally
senses.definition: to employ a lawyer or other professional and give them instructions, in legal usage
senses.definitionCN: 法律用法中委托律师等专业人员并给予指示
senses.example: They instructed a solicitor to write the will.
senses.exampleCN: 他们委托一位事务律师起草遗嘱。
senses.why: The order becomes a professional engagement: you instruct the person who acts for you.
senses.whyCN: 「吩咐」变成专业委托：你指示替你办事的人。

intro.en: Instruct comes from Latin instruere "to build in, equip, teach", built on struere "to pile up, build".
intro.cn: instruct 来自拉丁语 instruere「在内部建造、装备、教导」，基于 struere「堆积、建造」。

items.en: Struere "to pile up, build" is the root behind structure and construct.
items.cn: struere「堆积、建造」是 structure、construct 的词根。

items.en: In- plus struere gave instruere, "to build in, arrange, equip, teach".
items.cn: in- 加 struere 得到 instruere，意为「在内部建造、安排、装备、教导」。

items.en: The past participle instructus meant "equipped, taught".
items.cn: 过去分词 instructus 意为「被装备的、被教导的」。

items.en: Old French instruire passed the verb to English in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 instruire 在十五世纪把这一动词传入英语。

items.en: The "give orders" sense develops from the idea of telling someone what to carry out.
items.cn: 「下命令」义从「告诉某人要执行什么」发展而来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -struct- building stem; the near-meaning group holds other verbs of teaching and ordering.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -struct-「建造」词干；近义组收其他表示「教」与「命令」的动词。

entries.definition: The person who instructs, an agent noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「教练、讲师」，是施事名词。

entries.definition: To build, with con- meaning together.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「建造」，前缀 con- 表「共同」。

entries.definition: The way something is built.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「结构」，即建造的方式。

entries.definition: The general word for helping someone learn.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「教」，最一般。

entries.definition: To tell someone firmly to do something, sharper than instruct.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「命令」，比 instruct 更强硬。

entries.definition: To tell someone how to get somewhere or what to do, more general.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「指引」，更宽泛。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the building root struct- and split the teaching sense from the ordering sense.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子利用「建造」词根 struct-，并把「教」与「命令」两义分开。

normal.en: struct- is to build: instruct is building knowledge inside someone.
normal.cn: struct- 是建造：instruct 就是在人心里搭起知识。

normal.en: Instructor, structure, construct all share the stem.
normal.cn: instructor、structure、construct 共享词干。

normal.en: Instruct someone to wait means telling them officially.
normal.cn: instruct someone to wait 指正式吩咐他等待。

normal.en: As instructed means exactly as you were told.
normal.cn: as instructed 意为「按指示照做」。

normal.en: A judge instructs the jury at the end of a trial.
normal.cn: 法官在审判结束时向陪审团作指示。

abstract.en: Think of a coach arranging steps in the air like bricks.
abstract.cn: 想象教练把步骤像砖一样在空中码好。

abstract.en: Every instruction is a small building left in the mind.
abstract.cn: 每条说明都是留在心里的一座小建筑。

abstract.en: To instruct well is to make the next step obvious.
abstract.cn: 教得好，就是让下一步变得显而易见。

examples.en: The nurse instructed us how to change the bandage.
examples.cn: 护士教我们如何更换绷带。

examples.en: We were instructed to wait outside the door.
examples.cn: 我们被吩咐在门外等候。

examples.en: He instructs evening classes in basic electronics.
examples.cn: 他教基础电子学的晚间课程。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因斯抓克特」——因为抓得紧、抓得准，才教得好

root: 拉丁语 struere「堆积、建造」→ in- + struere = instruere「在内部建造、装备、教导」→ 过去分词 instructus「被教导的」→ 古法语 instruire → 十五世纪英语 instruct；「下命令」义由「吩咐执行」引申。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: teaching a skill, giving an order, and formally engaging a professional.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：教授技能、下达指示，以及正式委托专业人士。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: steps are stacked like bricks and the learner copies each one.
core.cn: 核心意象：步骤像砖一样叠起，学习者照着一步步做。

branches.en: THE LESSON: skill is built into the learner.
branches.cn: 课堂这条线：技能被建进学习者身上。

branches.en: THE COURTROOM: a firm instruction given from authority.
branches.cn: 法庭这条线：由权力下达的明确指示。

branches.en: THE OFFICE: a solicitor is engaged with instructions.
branches.cn: 办公室这条线：带着指示委托律师。

branches.en: THE LINK: both put one person in the place of knowing more.
branches.cn: 连接线：两者都让某人处在「知道得更多」的位置。

branches.en: THE REGISTER: the professional sense is legal and formal.
branches.cn: 语域线：专业委托义属法律正式用法。

intro.en: Instruct is in- "in" plus the Latin building root stru-, with a participle stem.
intro.cn: instruct 是 in-「入」加拉丁「建造」词根 stru-，再带分词词干。

latinIntro.en: Latin struere, instruere and instructus are all recorded in classical texts.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 struere、instruere、instructus 均在古典文献中有记载。

items.example: The building happens inside the learner.
items.exampleCN: 建造发生在学习者内部。

items.example: The compound is the direct source.
Instruction names both teaching and orders.
