The bare stem survives as a noun.
items.exampleCN: 无前缀词干作为名词留存。

definition_zh: 反常的；异常的；不正常的；不合规范的
definition_en: different from what is usual, expected or considered normal, often in a way that causes concern
core_image: 一把本该方正的木尺歪了一角，量出来的线全跟着偏
scene: 体检报告上有一项指标远远超出参考范围，医生反复看了两遍。 The scan showed an abnormal growth in the patient's left lung.
sceneCN: 这里 abnormal 是「异常的、偏离正常范围的」（第 2 个义项：医学指标超出正常范围）；句意为扫描显示病人左肺有一处异常增生。

pos.zh: 反常的；异常的；不正常的
反常的人或事物（较少使用）

derivatives.zh: 由 abnormal 加 -ly 构成副词，义为「异常地；反常地」
由 abnormal 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「异常；畸形」
abnormal 的肯定对应形式，义为「正常的；标准的」

senses.title: Departing from what is usual
senses.definition: differing from the ordinary or expected pattern of things
senses.definitionCN: 与平常或预期的模式不同
senses.example: An abnormal silence fell over the usually noisy hall.
senses.exampleCN: 平日喧闹的大厅里出现了一阵反常的寂静。
senses.why: Latin norma was a carpenter's square, the rule by which things are measured straight; ab- takes the measure away.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 norma 是本工用的曲尺，是量正东西的准绳；ab- 把这条准绳拿走，量出来的就偏了。

senses.title: Outside the medical reference range
senses.titleCN: 医学指标超出正常范围
senses.definition: of a test value or body condition, falling outside the range considered healthy
senses.definitionCN: 检查数值或身体状况落在健康范围之外
senses.example: The blood test returned an abnormal reading for iron.
senses.exampleCN: 血液检查的铁含量读数异常。
senses.why: Medicine applies the same square to the body: a reading off the healthy line is flagged as abnormal.
senses.whyCN: 医学把同一把尺子用在身体上：读数偏离健康线，就被标为异常。

senses.title: Socially or morally deviant
senses.definition: departing from accepted social or moral standards in a way others notice
senses.definitionCN: 偏离被接受的社会或道德标准，并为他人察觉
senses.example: Neighbours called his abnormal habits a public nuisance.
senses.exampleCN: 邻居把他反常的习惯称为公害。
senses.why: The square is also a social rule; behaviour that will not line up with it is judged deviant.
senses.whyCN: 这把尺子也是社会规范；对不齐的行为就会被判为越轨。

senses.title: Unusually large or small in degree
senses.definition: markedly greater or smaller in amount or intensity than is typical
senses.definitionCN: 在数量或强度上明显大于或小于通常水平
senses.example: An abnormal demand for ice cleared every shelf in the shop.
senses.exampleCN: 异常旺盛的冰块需求把店里的货架清空了。
senses.why: Beyond the rule is not only wrong but extreme: the measure has moved far from the centre.
senses.whyCN: 超出准绳不只是错，还意味着极端：刻度已经离中心很远。

senses.title: Irregular in structure or form
senses.definition: having a shape, structure or pattern that departs from the regular form
senses.definitionCN: 形状、结构或图案偏离规则形态
senses.example: The crystal showed an abnormal pattern under the microscope.
senses.exampleCN: 这块晶体在显微镜下呈现不规则的花样。
senses.why: Norma is literally a shape-making square, so a form that will not square up is abnormal.
senses.whyCN: norma 本义就是定形的曲尺，形状对不上这把尺，就是异常。

senses.title: Statistically atypical
senses.definition: lying far from the centre of a distribution or outside the expected range of data
senses.definitionCN: 远离分布中心或落在预期数据范围之外
senses.example: The model flagged an abnormal spike in traffic at midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 模型标出了午夜流量的异常尖峰。
senses.why: The rule becomes a statistical baseline; a point off that baseline is what the model calls abnormal.
senses.whyCN: 准绳变成统计基线；偏离基线的点，模型就称为异常。

senses.title: Worrying in behaviour or mood
senses.titleCN: 行为或情绪上令人担忧
senses.definition: showing behaviour or emotional responses that suggest a disorder needing attention
senses.definitionCN: 表现出提示某种障碍、需要关注的行为或情绪反应
senses.example: The teacher reported abnormal withdrawal in the child.
senses.exampleCN: 老师报告了这个孩子反常的退缩表现。
senses.why: When behaviour falls away from the expected line, the observer fears something is wrong inside.
senses.whyCN: 当行为偏离预期的那条线，观察者就会担心里面出了问题。

senses.title: Outside the normal course of development
senses.definition: of growth or development, following a course that is not the usual one
senses.definitionCN: 在生长或发展上走了一条并非通常的路线
senses.example: The doctor monitored the child's abnormal development closely.
senses.exampleCN: 医生密切监测这个孩子异常发育的情况。
senses.why: Development has an expected line of growth; a branch off that line is measured against the same square.
senses.whyCN: 发育有一条预期的生长线；从这条线岔出去，同样要拿这把尺来量。

intro.en: Abnormal is a modern word built on Latin norma, the square used to keep lines straight, and it has a Greek cousin in anomaly.
intro.cn: abnormal 是一个建立在拉丁语 norma「定线曲尺」之上的现代词，它在希腊语一侧还有个近亲 anomaly。

items.en: Norma meant a carpenter's square and, figuratively, a rule or standard. Its deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: norma 指木工的曲尺，引申为规则与标准；它更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Normalis meant made according to the square, hence regular or standard; English normal comes from it.
items.cn: normalis 意为「按曲尺做成的」，引申为规则的、标准的；英语 normal 由此而来。

items.en: Greek anomalos meant uneven or irregular, and it produced the separate English word anomaly.
items.cn: 希腊语 anomalos 意为「不平整的、不规则的」，后来产生另一个英语词 anomaly。

items.en: French formed anormal in the early nineteenth century; some accounts link it to the Greek word rather than to Latin norma.
items.cn: 法语在十九世纪初造出 anormal；有说法认为它上承希腊语那个词，而非拉丁语 norma，两种解释并存。

items.en: English abnormal appears in the 1810s and 1820s. The exact first date is uncertain, and the word spread with medical and statistical writing.
items.cn: 英语 abnormal 见于十九世纪一十至二十年代；确切首见年代不确定，这个词随医学与统计写作传播开来。

items.en: The word moved from anatomy and medicine into psychology, statistics and ordinary speech about behaviour.
items.cn: 这个词从解剖学与医学走进心理学、统计学，以及日常对行为的谈论。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on norma, including one word that hides the same root; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of deviation.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在 norma 之上的形式，其中包括一个隐藏着同一词根的词；近义组收表示「偏离」的形容词。

entries.definition: In an abnormal manner or to an abnormal degree.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「异常地、反常地」，由本词加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: The state of being abnormal, or an abnormal feature.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「异常、畸形」，由本词加 -ity 构成。

entries.definition: Conforming to the usual standard; the positive counterpart of abnormal.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「正常的、标准的」，是 abnormal 的肯定对应词，同出 norma。

entries.definition: Extremely large; it comes from Latin enormis, literally outside the square.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「巨大的」，出自拉丁语 enormis「离开曲尺的」，与本词共享 norma 词根。

entries.definition: Something that deviates from the standard; it comes from Greek anomalos, not from Latin norma.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「异常事物」，出自希腊语 anomalos；与 abnormal 意义接近，但词源不同。

entries.definition: Not common or ordinary; neutral and without the concern that abnormal can carry.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不寻常的」，语气中性，不像 abnormal 那样常带担忧。

entries.definition: Not representative of a type or group; common in medical and technical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「非典型的」，多用于医学与技术写作。

entries.definition: Not following a regular pattern in time, shape or occurrence.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不规则的」，强调时间、形状或出现方式上没有规律。

entries.definition: Departing from the accepted course, especially in biology or behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「偏离常规的」，语气正式，多用于生物学或行为描述。

entries.definition: A very unusual event or thing; informal and often harsh when applied to people.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「反常的（事物）」，口语用词，用于人时带有冒犯意味。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin norma, the square that keeps lines true.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的拉丁语 norma，也就是让线条保持平直的那把曲尺。

normal.en: Norma is a square: normal lines follow it, abnormal lines do not.
normal.cn: norma 是一把曲尺：正常的线顺着它走，反常的线对不上它。

normal.en: Normal is the positive twin; abnormal simply puts ab- in front.
normal.cn: normal 是它的肯定孪生词；abnormal 只是在前面加了 ab-。

normal.en: Enormous hides the same square: enormis meant outside the rule, and great things seemed to be outside it.
normal.cn: enormous 藏着同一把尺：enormis 意为「离开规则的」，巨大的东西看起来就在规则之外。

normal.en: Abnormal psychology studies behaviour measured against a social baseline.
normal.cn: abnormal psychology 研究的是拿社会基线来衡量的行为。

normal.en: An abnormal test result is a reading that will not lie on the healthy line.
normal.cn: abnormal 的检查结果就是落不到健康线上的读数。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler laid across a drawing: one line bends away, and the eye finds it at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺横放在图样上：有一条线弯开了，眼睛立刻就能找到它。

abstract.en: The same ruler measures bodies, behaviour, crystals and data.
abstract.cn: 同一把尺可以量身体、行为、晶体和数据。

abstract.en: Abnormal is not simply rare: it means far enough from the line that someone has to take notice.
abstract.cn: abnormal 不只是稀少：它意味着离那条线远到必须有人注意。

examples.en: The doctor ordered more tests after an abnormal result.
examples.cn: 结果异常后，医生安排了更多检查。

examples.en: Such abnormal weather is rare in this region.
examples.cn: 这样的异常天气在本地区很罕见。

examples.en: The machine shut down when it detected abnormal pressure.
examples.cn: 机器检测到异常压力后停机。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿布诺莫」——尺子一歪，量出来的全是怪数：反常、异常

root: 现代英语 abnormal 由否定前缀 ab- 加 normal 构成；normal 出自拉丁语 norma「木工曲尺、准则」与 normalis「按曲尺做成的」。希腊语 anomalos「不平整」是另一条词源线，产生英语 anomaly。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses of abnormal all measure something against a line: ordinary expectation, a healthy range, a social rule, a normal degree, a regular shape, a statistical baseline, expected behaviour, and a normal course of growth.
sensesIntro.cn: abnormal 的八个义项都在拿某样东西去对一条线：通常预期、健康范围、社会规范、正常程度、规则形状、统计基线、预期行为，以及正常发育路线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a square is laid on a drawing and one line refuses to follow it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把曲尺放在图样上，有一条线偏偏不肯顺着它。

branches.en: THE PATTERN: ordinary expectation and ordinary degree are the baseline the word departs from.
branches.cn: 模式线：通常预期与通常程度是这个词偏离的基线。

branches.en: THE NUMBER: medicine and statistics both read a value that falls outside the accepted range.
branches.cn: 数值线：医学与统计都在读一个落在可接受范围之外的数值。

branches.en: THE PERSON: social rule and emotional expectation judge behaviour that worries others.
branches.cn: 人的线：社会规范与情绪预期都在评判令他人担忧的行为。

branches.en: THE SHAPE: the square is literal here, and a form that will not square up is irregular.
branches.cn: 形状线：这里曲尺是本义，对不上尺的形状就是不规则的。

branches.en: THE COURSE: development has a line of its own, and a branch away from it is abnormal.
branches.cn: 进程线：发育有自己的路线，从这条线岔出去就是异常。

intro.en: Abnormal is a prefix plus a Latin-derived adjective; English adds -ly and -ity to complete the set.
intro.cn: abnormal 是一个前缀加一个来自拉丁语的形容词；英语再加 -ly 与 -ity 补全这一组词。

latinIntro.en: Latin norma and normalis are recorded; the deeper origin of norma is source uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 norma 与 normalis 有文献记录，norma 更早的来源不确定。

items.example: The prefix marks distance from the rule.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记与规则的偏离。

items.example: The square kept the timber straight.

items.exampleCN: 它构成 normal 与 abnormal。

items.meaningCN: 离开准则的，因而巨大的
items.exampleCN: 这个词产生了英语 enormous。

items.example: It produced the separate word anomaly.
items.exampleCN: 它产生了另一个词 anomaly。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「异常地」
由本词加 -ity 构成，义为「异常；畸形」
与本词同根的肯定形式，义为「正常的」

definition_zh: 航空邮件；航空邮递；航空邮资
definition_en: mail carried by aircraft, the service that carries it, or the postage charged for it
core_image: 一只薄薄的信封，边角印着蓝红相间的斜纹
scene: 邮局柜台上摆着两种信封，一种边角印着蓝红斜纹。 She sent the documents by airmail so they would arrive before the deadline.
sceneCN: 这里 airmail 是「航空邮递」（第 2 个义项：用航空方式寄送邮件）；句意为她把这些文件寄了航空件，好在截止日期前送到。

pos.zh: 名词：航空邮件；航空邮递；航空邮资

derivatives.zh: 由本词加后缀 -er 构成，义为「航空邮件；寄航空信的人」
由本词加名词后缀 -ing 构成，义为「航空寄送」

senses.title: Mail carried by aircraft
senses.definition: letters and parcels sent by aircraft instead of by ship or road
senses.definitionCN: 用航空器而非船只或陆路寄送的信件与包裹
senses.example: The airmail arrived two days earlier than the surface post.
senses.exampleCN: 航空邮件比平邮早到了两天。
senses.why: Air names the carrier and mail names what is carried, so the compound names the post itself.
senses.whyCN: air 指出运载方式，mail 指出所运之物，这个复合词因此指邮件本身。

senses.title: The service of sending mail by air
senses.definition: the postal service that uses aircraft to move mail quickly between places
senses.definitionCN: 利用航空器在各地点之间快速运送邮件的邮政业务
senses.example: She sent the documents by airmail so they would arrive before the deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 她把这些文件寄了航空件，好在截止日期前送到。
senses.why: The phrase by airmail names the method, so the compound also stands for the service that provides it.
senses.whyCN: 短语 by airmail 指的是一种方式，因此这个复合词也代表提供这种方式的服务。

senses.title: The postage charged for air transport
senses.definition: the higher rate paid for sending something by aircraft
senses.definitionCN: 为航空寄送所付的较高邮资
senses.example: The airmail rate went up again this spring.
senses.exampleCN: 今年春天航空邮资又涨了。
senses.why: Once a service exists, its price needs a name, and the compound supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 一项业务一旦存在，它的价格就需要一个名称，这个复合词正好提供。

intro.en: Airmail joins two English words: air for the method of carriage and mail for the letters themselves.
intro.cn: airmail 由两个英语词组成：air 指运送方式，mail 指信件本身。

items.en: Male meant a bag or a wallet, and mail first named the bag that carried letters.
items.cn: 古法语 male 意为「袋子、皮包」，mail 最初指装信件的袋子。

items.en: Mail came to mean the letters and parcels themselves, and later the system that moves them.
items.cn: mail 后来指信件与包裹本身，再后来指运送它们的系统。

items.en: Air plus mail appears as aircraft began carrying post; the exact first use is uncertain, and the compound spread with international services.
items.cn: 随着航空器开始运送邮件，air 与 mail 组合出现；确切首用年代不确定，这一复合词随国际邮政业务普及。

items.en: Airmail envelopes, rates, and labels became standard objects of everyday life.
items.cn: 航空信封、航空邮资与航空标签成了日常生活中的常见物件。

items.en: Electronic mail reduced the everyday use of the word, and airmail now mostly survives in postal and historical contexts.
items.cn: 电子邮件减少了这个词的日常使用，如今 airmail 多保留在邮政与历史语境中。

note.en: The look-alike group is built from airmail; the near-meaning group gathers other words for post and delivery.
note.cn: 形近组由 airmail 构成；近义组收其他表示邮政与投递的词。

entries.definition: A letter or packet sent by air, or a person who sends one.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「航空邮件；寄航空信的人」，由本词加后缀构成。

entries.definition: The act of sending something by air mail.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「航空寄送」，指用航空邮件方式寄出。

entries.definition: The light envelope with striped edges used for air mail.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「航空信封」，指边角印有斜纹的薄信封。

entries.definition: Mail carried by ship, road, or rail rather than by air.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「平邮、水陆邮件」，指经船运、陆运而非航空运送的邮件。

entries.definition: The system and the letters it handles, without saying how they travel.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「邮政、邮件」，不说明运送方式。

entries.definition: Letters and parcels, or the service that delivers them; the base of airmail.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「邮件、邮政」，是 airmail 的基础词。

entries.definition: A company or person that delivers items quickly and directly.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「快递、信使」，指快速直接投递物品的公司或人。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the bag origin of mail and the phrases airmail appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用 mail 的「袋子」来源，以及 airmail 实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Mail first meant the bag that held letters, then the letters, then the system.
normal.cn: mail 先指装信的袋子，再指信，最后指整个邮政系统。

normal.en: Airmail is mail that travels by air, so the modifier tells you the carrier, not the contents.
normal.cn: airmail 是走航空的邮件，修饰语说明的是运载方式，而不是内容。

normal.en: By airmail names the method; airmail rate names the price of that method.
normal.cn: by airmail 指方式；airmail rate 指这种方式的价钱。

normal.en: The striped airmail envelope is thin because every gram costs money in the air.
normal.cn: 航空信封做得薄，因为在天上每一克都要算钱。

normal.en: Surface mail is the direct opposite: it goes by ship, road, or rail.
normal.cn: surface mail 正好相反：走海运、陆运或铁路。

abstract.en: Picture a thin striped envelope lying on a counter beside a heavier plain one.
abstract.cn: 想象柜台上放着一只薄薄的斜纹信封，旁边是一只更厚的普通信封。

abstract.en: The stripes mark a decision: this one will fly instead of sail.
abstract.cn: 那些斜纹标记着一个决定：这一只要飞，而不是走海路。

abstract.en: Speed is what the stripes buy, and the higher rate is what speed costs.
abstract.cn: 斜纹买到的是速度，而更高的邮资就是速度的代价。

examples.en: She sent the documents by airmail so they would arrive before the deadline.
examples.cn: 她把这些文件寄了航空件，好在截止日期前送到。

examples.en: The airmail arrived two days earlier than the surface post.
examples.cn: 航空邮件比平邮早到了两天。

examples.en: The airmail rate went up again this spring.
examples.cn: 今年春天航空邮资又涨了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱尔，妹儿」——让信飞着去找人：航空邮件

root: 英语 air 与 mail 的复合。mail 经古法语 male「袋子」进入英语，先指装信件的袋子，后指信件与邮政系统；二十世纪初航空器开始运送邮件，air 加 mail 的组合随之出现，并固定出航空信封、航空邮资等说法。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses separate what is sent, how it is sent, and what the sending costs: the mail itself, the air service, and the air rate.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项把寄的东西、寄的方式与寄的价钱分开：邮件本身、航空业务，以及航空邮资。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin envelope with blue and red stripes along its edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只薄薄的信封，边角印着蓝红相间的斜纹。

branches.en: THE LETTERS: the compound first names the mail that flies.
branches.cn: 信件线：这个复合词首先指走航空的那些邮件。

branches.en: THE SERVICE: by airmail names a method, and the method stands for the organisation behind it.
branches.cn: 业务线：by airmail 指的是一种方式，这种方式又代表背后的机构。

branches.en: THE PRICE: speed has a cost, and the cost takes the name of the service.
branches.cn: 价格线：速度有代价，这个代价沿用了业务的名称。

branches.en: THE SAME WORD: what is sent and how it is sent are one compound seen from two sides.
branches.cn: 同词线：寄什么与怎么寄，是同一个复合词的两个侧面。

branches.en: THE COUNTER: at the post office the service and its rate are quoted in one breath.
branches.cn: 柜台线：在邮局，业务与资费总是被一起报价。

intro.en: Airmail is a native compound, and English adds -er and -ing to name the sender and the act.
intro.cn: airmail 是英语本族复合词，英语用 -er 与 -ing 指寄件者与寄送行为。

latinIntro.en: Both halves are native or Old French in origin, so the Latin entries remain empty.
latinIntro.cn: 两个成分分别源自英语本族与古法语，因此拉丁条目留空。

items.example: The post now travels by air.
Male is the source of mail.
items.exampleCN: male 是 mail 的来源。

items.example: The second half names what is carried.
items.exampleCN: 后半部分指出所运之物。

items.example: Send it by airmail if it is urgent.

items.meaning: mail carried by land or sea
items.example: Surface mail is cheaper but slower.
The airmail rate depends on weight.

derivatives.zh: 由本词加后缀构成，义为「航空邮件」
由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「航空寄送」

definition_zh: 王国；国度；（生物分类的）界；领域
definition_en: a country ruled by a king or queen, and by extension a whole domain such as living things or a field of activity
core_image: 地图上一大片被围起来的疆土，界线外写着别人的名字
scene: 旧地图摊在桌上，纸边已经卷起。 That kingdom once reached from the mountains to the sea.
sceneCN: 这里 kingdom 是「王国」（第 1 个义项：由国王或女王统治的国家），句意是那个王国当时从山区一直延伸到海边。画面里有摊开的旧地图、卷起的纸边和海岸线。

pos.zh: 领域；王国（喻某事物自成一体）

derivatives.zh: 与 kingdom 同后缀 -dom 的词，指自由，说明该后缀表示状态
duke 加 -dom 构成，指公爵领地，同一模式的其他爵位
kingdom 加 wide 合成，指全国范围的

senses.title: A country ruled by a monarch
senses.definition: a state whose head is a king or a queen
senses.definitionCN: 以国王或女王为国家元首的国家
senses.example: The kingdom lasted more than six hundred years.
senses.exampleCN: 这个王国延续了六百多年。
senses.why: The suffix -dom names a realm or a condition, so king plus -dom names the place a king holds.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -dom 表示领域或状态，因此 king 加 -dom 就是国王所辖的地方。

senses.title: A monarchy as a political form
senses.definition: a country with a monarch as its constitutional form of government
senses.definitionCN: 以君主为政体的国家形式
senses.example: Three kingdoms share that island.
senses.exampleCN: 那座岛上共有三个君主国。
senses.why: When the word names a political form rather than a person's land, it enters the language of constitutions.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词指政体而非某人的土地时，它就进入了宪法的语汇。

senses.title: One of the great divisions of living things
senses.definition: the highest rank in the traditional classification of living things
senses.definitionCN: 传统生物分类中的最高等级
senses.example: Fungi form their own kingdom.
senses.exampleCN: 真菌自成一大界。
senses.why: Classification needed a word for the top level, and the royal realm supplied a natural image of rank.
senses.whyCN: 分类学需要为最高层级找一个词，而王国的疆域恰好提供了等级的自然意象。

senses.title: A separate world of its own
senses.definition: an area of activity or interest that feels like a closed world
senses.definitionCN: 感觉像一个封闭世界的活动或兴趣范围
senses.example: The old bookshop is a kingdom of paper and dust.
senses.exampleCN: 那家旧书店是纸与灰自成一体的小天地。
senses.why: A kingdom has its own law and borders, so any self-contained world can be called one.
senses.whyCN: 王国自成法律与边界，因此任何自成一体的世界都能这样称呼。

senses.title: The realm of God or the dead
senses.definition: a religious name for the realm of God or of the dead
senses.definitionCN: 宗教用语，指上帝所辖或亡者所在的世界
senses.example: The prayer asks for the kingdom to come.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇祈祷文祈求天国降临。
senses.why: Religion borrowed the political word to speak of a rule that is not of this world.
senses.whyCN: 宗教借用了政治词来描述一种不属于此世的统治。

intro.en: Kingdom is a native compound: the old word for a clan head joined to a Germanic suffix that names a state or a realm.
intro.cn: kingdom 是本土复合词：表示氏族首领的旧词接上表示状态或领域的日耳曼后缀。

items.en: The suffix appears in Germanic as -domaz, naming a condition, a rank, or a jurisdiction.
items.cn: 这个后缀在日耳曼语中作 -domaz，表示状态、身份或管辖范围。

items.en: Old English had cyningdom, the domain of a cyning, and the suffix was -dom.
items.cn: 古英语已有 cyningdom，指 cyning（王）的辖地，后缀作 -dom。

items.en: Religious texts used the word for the rule of God, giving the kingdom of heaven.
items.cn: 宗教文本用这个词指上帝的统治，产生了「天国」的说法。

items.en: The form settled as kingdom and the plural took -s.
items.cn: 词形固定为 kingdom，复数加 -s。

items.en: Biology adopted the word for its highest rank of living things in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 十八世纪生物学采用这个词指生物的最高分类级。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the -dom family and the king root; the near-meaning group holds other words for a state or a realm.
note.cn: 形近组收 -dom 词族与 king 词根；近义组收其他表示国家或领域的词。

entries.definition: The ruler whose realm this word names.
entries.definitionCN: 指国王，也就是这个词所指疆域的统治者。

entries.definition: A duke's territory, the same pattern one rank lower.
entries.definitionCN: 指公爵领，是同一模式下的低一级。

entries.definition: The same -dom naming a state rather than a place.
entries.definitionCN: 同样带 -dom，但表示状态而非地方。

entries.definition: An earl's rank and land, another rank in the same series.
entries.definitionCN: 指伯爵的身份与封地，同一序列的另一级。

entries.definition: A group of states under one supreme ruler.
entries.definitionCN: 指由一位至高统治者统辖的多个国家。

entries.definition: A people and their country, whether monarchical or not.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个民族及其国家，不论是否有君主。

entries.definition: A kingdom, and also any field of activity.
entries.definitionCN: 指王国，也可指任何活动领域。

entries.definition: A state with an elected head, the reverse of a monarchy.
entries.definitionCN: 指元首经选举产生的国家，与君主国相对。

normalIntro.en: These hooks join the king root to the suffix for a realm, then follow the word into biology and religion.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把 king 词根接上表示领域的后缀，再把它带进生物学与宗教。

normal.en: -Dom names a state or a realm, as in freedom and dukedom.
normal.cn: -dom 表示状态或领域，如 freedom 与 dukedom。

normal.en: United Kingdom is the fixed name for Britain in official use.
normal.cn: United Kingdom 是英国在正式场合的固定名称。

normal.en: Animal kingdom is the top division of animals in old classification.
normal.cn: animal kingdom 是旧分类中动物的最高一级。

normal.en: Kingdom and king differ only by the suffix.
normal.cn: kingdom 与 king 只差一个后缀。

normal.en: The plural is kingdoms, never kingdomes.
normal.cn: 复数是 kingdoms，不写 kingdomes。

abstract.en: A kingdom is a line drawn around people who accept one name.
abstract.cn: 王国就是画在一群认可同一个名字的人外面的那条线。

abstract.en: Every field that feels complete becomes a kingdom of its own.
abstract.cn: 任何自成一体的领域都会变成它自己的王国。

abstract.en: Biology borrowed a throne to sort living things into great halls.
abstract.cn: 生物学借来一张王座，把生物分进几个大堂。

examples.en: The kingdom was divided among three brothers.
examples.cn: 这个王国被三个兄弟分了。

examples.en: Insects make up most of the animal kingdom.
examples.cn: 昆虫占了动物界的大部分。

examples.en: That garden is her own small kingdom.
examples.cn: 那座花园是她自己的小王国。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「king 的母」——国王的地盘就叫王国

root: 古英语 cyningdom，由 cyning（王，源出日耳曼语「族人头领」）加后缀 -dom（表示状态、领域）构成；后由具体疆土扩为政体名、生物分类的最高一级及喻义的「领域」。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: a monarch's country, monarchy as a political form, the top rank in biology, a self-contained world, and the religious realm.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：君主所治的国家、作为政体的君主国、生物分类的最高一级、自成一体的小天地，以及宗教上的国度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a border drawn around the land one name rules.
core.cn: 核心意象：围绕一个名字所辖之地画下的一条界线。

branches.en: THE MAP LINE: a country and the constitutional form it takes.
branches.cn: 地图这条线：一个国家以及它的政体形式。

branches.en: THE CLASSIFICATION LINE: rank borrowed for living things.
branches.cn: 分类这条线：借用等级来给生物排序。

branches.en: THE INNER LINE: a world small enough to hold in one room.
branches.cn: 内心这条线：小到能装进一间屋子的世界。

branches.en: THE PRAYER LINE: a rule not of this world.
branches.cn: 祈祷这条线：不属于此世的统治。

branches.en: THE BORDER LINE: every kingdom is defined by what lies outside.
branches.cn: 边界这条线：每个王国都由界外之物来界定。

intro.en: The word is a root plus a Germanic suffix, and the suffix is the lesson: it builds freedom, dukedom, and earldom the same way.
intro.cn: 这个词是词根加日耳曼后缀，真正值得学的是后缀：它同样造出 freedom、dukedom、earldom。

latinIntro.en: Neither part is Latin, so the entries below are only Latin words for a kingdom or a rule, given for contrast.
latinIntro.cn: 两个部分都不来自拉丁语，下面列出的只是表示王国或统治的拉丁词，作对照用。

items.exampleCN: 这个王国只有一条大路。
他的君王气度令人印象深刻。

items.example: The dukedom passed to a cousin.
items.exampleCN: 公爵领地传给了一位堂亲。
一道全国性的敕令被宣读。

items.example: The United Kingdom has four parts.
items.exampleCN: 联合王国由四部分组成。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 拉丁语「统治权、帝国」，与 kingdom 意义相近而制度不同

definition_zh: 木制的；木头的；僵硬的；呆板的；生硬的
definition_en: made of wood, or stiff and unnatural in movement or manner
core_image: 一只雕得正好的木手，纹路对，可是弯不下去
scene: 旧教堂里那排椅子全是硬木做的，坐上去一动就会响。 The actor gave a wooden performance that made the whole audience sit still.
sceneCN: 这里 wooden 是「木制的」（第 1 个义项：用木头做成的）；句意是那个演员演得呆板僵硬，让全场观众都坐得直直的。雕得正好却弯不下去的木手，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 wooden 加 -ly 构成，义为「呆板地；僵硬地」
由 wooden 加 -ness 构成，义为「呆板；僵硬」
去掉 -en 得到的名词，义为「木材；树林」

senses.title: Made of timber
senses.definition: made from the hard material of a tree, especially for furniture or tools
senses.definitionCN: 用树木的坚硬材料制成，尤指家具或工具
senses.example: The long rows of seats in the old church were wooden and squeaked.
senses.exampleCN: 老教堂里那排长长的座椅都是木制的，一坐就吱呀响。
senses.why: The old ending -en means made of, so the material name becomes an adjective of substance.
senses.whyCN: 古老的词尾 -en 表示「由……制成」，于是材料名变成了表示材质的形容词。

senses.title: Stiff like dead timber
senses.definition: moving or bending awkwardly, as if the body had no joints
senses.definitionCN: 动作笨拙生硬，像身体没有关节一样
senses.example: His wooden movements at the dance made everyone smile.
senses.exampleCN: 他在舞会上僵硬的舞步让大家都会心一笑。
senses.why: Wood does not bend, so a person who moves like a board is described with the same word.
senses.whyCN: 木头不会弯，因此动作像木板的人就用同一个词来形容。

senses.title: Unnatural in manner
senses.definition: stiff and without warmth in voice, expression or performance
senses.definitionCN: 声音、表情或表演僵硬而没有温度
senses.example: The actor gave a wooden performance that made the whole audience sit still.
senses.exampleCN: 那个演员演得呆板僵硬，让全场观众都坐得直直的。
senses.why: From bodies the meaning spreads to manner: a face or a voice that shows no living change is wooden too.
senses.whyCN: 从身体延伸到举止：一张不会变化的脸、一个不起伏的声音同样是 wooden。

intro.en: Wooden is the Old English noun wudu with the old adjective ending -en, which says made of.
intro.cn: wooden 是古英语名词 wudu 加上古老的形容词词尾 -en，意思是「由……制成」。

items.en: wudu was the material, and the ending -en marked a thing made of it.
items.cn: wudu 是那种材料，词尾 -en 标注由它制成的东西。

items.en: The same ending built golden and silken, which is why the forms look alike.
items.cn: 同一个词尾也造出 golden 与 silken，所以这些形式看起来很相似。

items.en: The form settled as wooden, and the unstressed ending lost its vowel sound.
items.cn: 形式固定为 wooden，非重读的词尾失去了元音的音值。

items.en: The literal sense held, and the figurative sense of stiff followed naturally.
items.cn: 字面义保留，僵硬这一比喻义随之自然出现。

items.en: Today the adjective describes acting and speech as often as furniture.
items.cn: 今天这个形容词形容表演和说话，几乎和形容家具一样频繁。

note.en: The first group holds other words ending in the old made-of suffix, the second holds adjectives of stiffness.
note.cn: 第一组收其他带「由……制成」这个词尾的词，第二组收表示僵硬的形容词。

entries.definition: The material of trees.
entries.definitionCN: 木材

entries.definition: Full of wood or trees.
entries.definitionCN: 木质化的；树木茂密的

entries.definition: Made of gold, or gold in colour.
entries.definitionCN: 金的；金色的

entries.definition: Hard to bend, or not relaxed.
entries.definitionCN: 僵硬的；不自然的

entries.definition: Fixed and unable to bend.
entries.definitionCN: 僵直的；僵硬不变的

entries.definition: Showing no energy or feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 无生气的；呆滞的

normalIntro.en: Wooden is wood plus the old -en that means made of, the same ending as in golden.
normalIntro.cn: wooden 是 wood 加表示「由……制成」的古老 -en，与 golden 的词尾相同。

normal.en: Wood plus en gives wooden, with no extra letter dropped.
normal.cn: wood 加 en 就是 wooden，中间不落字母。

normal.en: The ending -en means made of, as in golden and silken.
normal.cn: -en 表示「由……制成」，如 golden 与 silken。

normal.en: Because it already ends in -en, the comparison uses more wooden.
normal.cn: 因为它以 -en 结尾，比较级用 more wooden。

normal.en: Woodenly adds -ly for the manner, woodenness adds -ness for the state.
normal.cn: woodenly 加 -ly 表示方式，woodenness 加 -ness 表示状态。

normal.en: A wooden face is a face like a board: flat, stiff, and giving nothing away.
normal.cn: wooden face 是像木板一样的脸：平坦、僵硬，什么都不透露。

abstract.en: A carved hand that cannot close its fingers.
abstract.cn: 一只雕好的手，手指合不上。

abstract.en: A door that opens with a long dry complaint.
abstract.cn: 一扇门打开时发出一声长长的干响。

abstract.en: A voice with no weather in it.
abstract.cn: 一个没有天气变化的声音。

examples.en: She stirred the soup with a wooden spoon and never let it boil.
examples.cn: 她用木勺搅着汤，从不让它滚起来。

examples.en: The dancer looked wooden because he was trying too hard.
examples.cn: 那位舞者显得僵硬，是因为他太使劲了。

examples.en: He answered in a wooden voice, like a person reading from a card.
examples.cn: 他生硬地回答，像在照着卡片念。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「屋登」——梯子是用木头做的，踩上去一级一级「噔」上去。

root: 古英语 wudu（木材）+ 后缀 -en（由……制成的，同 golden、silken）→ wooden；木不弯，故引申为「僵硬、呆板」。

sensesIntro.en: The adjective begins as a statement about material, then moves to bodies that will not bend, then to faces and voices with no change in them.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个形容词从说明材料开始，转到弯不了的身体，再转到毫无变化的脸和声音。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a carved hand that cannot close.
core.cn: 核心意象：雕好却合不上手指的木手。

branches.en: The material branch: rows of wooden seats in a church.
branches.cn: 材料分支：教堂里一排排木椅。

branches.en: The body branch: stiff steps on the dance floor.
branches.cn: 身体分支：舞池里僵硬的舞步。

branches.en: The manner branch: a wooden performance.
branches.cn: 举止分支：呆板的表演。

branches.en: The everyday branch: wooden describes tools and acting alike.
branches.cn: 日常分支：wooden 既形容工具也形容表演。

branches.en: The stiffness branch: from limbs that will not bend to a voice that will not rise.
branches.cn: 僵硬分支：从弯不了的肢体到起伏不了的声音。

intro.en: Wooden is a stem plus one suffix; the ending -en is the part that says made of.
intro.cn: wooden 是一个词干加一个后缀；说「由……制成」的正是 -en。

latinIntro.en: Both parts are native and Germanic; the Latin words below express the same made-of idea with a different ending.
latinIntro.cn: 两部分都是日耳曼语本土成分；下面的拉丁词用另一种词尾表达同样的「由……制成」。

items.exampleCN: 它由 wood 构成 wooden。

items.example: The suffix also builds wool words.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾也用于 wool 一族。

definition_zh: 平民；非军人；民用的
definition_en: a person who is not a member of the armed forces, or ordinary rather than military use
core_image: 穿便装的人站在一排军装之外
scene: 警报解除后，街上的人群慢慢散开。 Many civilians were hurt in the attack.
sceneCN: 这里 civilians 指「平民」（第 1 个义项：不属于武装部队的人）；句意是许多平民在这次袭击中受伤。

senses.title: A person not in the army
senses.definition: a person who is not a member of the armed forces
senses.definitionCN: 不属于武装部队的人
senses.example: Many civilians were hurt in the attack.
senses.exampleCN: 许多平民在这次袭击中受伤。
senses.why: French civilien named a person concerned with civil life rather than with war.
senses.whyCN: 法语 civilien 指关心民事生活而非战争的人。

senses.title: Ordinary rather than military
senses.definition: used for ordinary people rather than for soldiers
senses.definitionCN: 供普通人而非军人使用的
senses.example: The plane was sold for civilian use.
senses.exampleCN: 这架飞机被出售用于民用。
senses.why: The adjective applies the same civil and military contrast to objects.
senses.whyCN: 形容词把同样的民事与军事对比用在物品上。

intro.en: Civilian is a French word for someone who lives by civil rather than military rules.
intro.cn: civilian 是一个法语词，指按民事而非军事规则生活的人。

items.en: Civilis meant belonging to a citizen.
items.cn: civilis 意为属于公民的。

items.en: Civilien named a student of civil law.
items.cn: civilien 原指研习民法的人。

items.en: English civilian came to mean a person outside the army.
items.cn: 英语 civilian 转而指不在军队中的人。

items.en: The adjective sense extended to non military equipment.
items.cn: 形容词义扩展到非军事装备。

items.en: The word now marks the line between war and ordinary life.
items.cn: 这个词如今标记战争与日常生活之间的界线。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the civil stem, while the meaning group names people outside a conflict.
note.cn: 形近组共享 civil 词干，近义组列出冲突之外的人。

entries.definition: relating to citizens or to politeness
entries.definitionCN: 与公民或礼貌有关的

entries.definition: an advanced and organized society
entries.definitionCN: 发达而有组织的社会

entries.definition: a large and important town
entries.definitionCN: 规模大而重要的城镇

entries.definition: a person who does not take part in fighting
entries.definitionCN: 不参与战斗的人

entries.definition: a person who lives in a place
entries.definitionCN: 居住在某地的人

entries.definition: a legal member of a state
entries.definitionCN: 国家的法定成员

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the civil stem, the civilian clothes image and the war contrast.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用 civil 词干、便服意象以及与战争的对比。

normal.en: Civilian is civil plus -ian, so it names the person who lives under civil rules.
normal.cn: civilian 就是 civil 加 -ian，指按民事规则生活的人。

normal.en: Civilian clothes are everyday clothes, the opposite of a uniform.
normal.cn: civilian clothes 是日常便服，正是军装的反面。

normal.en: A civilian job is a job outside the army, in ordinary working life.
normal.cn: a civilian job 是军队之外的工作，属于普通职业生涯。

normal.en: Return to civilian life is the phrase used when a soldier leaves service.
normal.cn: return to civilian life 是军人退役时常用的说法。

normal.en: The plural civilians is common because wars harm whole populations.
normal.cn: 复数 civilians 很常见，因为战争会伤害整片人群。

abstract.en: Picture a man in a plain coat standing apart from a row of uniforms.
abstract.cn: 想象一个穿素色外套的人，站在一排队列军装之外。

abstract.en: Picture a family carrying bags along a road after a loud night.
abstract.cn: 想象一家人提着包走在路上，身后是嘈杂的一夜。

abstract.en: Picture a former soldier in a soft shirt learning a new trade.
abstract.cn: 想象一名退役士兵穿着软领衬衫学习新手艺。

examples.en: The army was ordered to protect civilians.
examples.cn: 军队奉命保护平民。

examples.en: After ten years he returned to civilian life.
examples.cn: 十年之后他回归了平民生活。

examples.en: The radar is now made for civilian use.
examples.cn: 这种雷达现在为民用而制造。

dict_mnemonic.text: civilian 就是 civil 加 -ian：过民事生活的人，就是平民。

root: 源自古法语 civilien，由拉丁语 civilis（公民的）派生，本指过民事生活而非军旅生活的人。

sensesIntro.en: A person of civil law becomes a person outside the army, and the contrast then extends to ordinary equipment.
sensesIntro.cn: 研习民法的人先变成军队之外的人，这种对比再扩展到普通器物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plain coat standing outside a row of uniforms.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件素色外套站在一排队列军装之外。

branches.en: The person outside the army is the central sense.
branches.cn: 军队之外的人是核心义项。

branches.en: The adjective carries the same line into objects.
branches.cn: 形容词把同一条界线带到物品上。

branches.en: A civilian person and civilian equipment share one contrast.
branches.cn: 平民与民用装备共享同一种对比。

branches.en: Civilians are defined by what they are not.
branches.cn: 平民是靠「不是什么」来定义的。

branches.en: Civilian use marks the peaceful side of a technology.
branches.cn: 民用标记出一项技术的和平一面。

intro.en: The stem builds a plural, a verb, an abstract noun and a slang clipping.
intro.cn: 这个词干构成复数、动词、抽象名词以及一个口语缩略词。

latinIntro.en: Old French civilien and Latin civilis supply both the base and the -ian ending.
latinIntro.cn: 古法语 civilien 与拉丁语 civilis 提供了词基与 -ian 词尾。

items.exampleCN: 一位平民拦下了那辆车。

items.meaningCN: 使转为平民或民用性质
items.example: The base was civilianized after the war.
items.exampleCN: 战后这座基地转为民用。

items.meaningCN: 平民化或民用化的过程
items.exampleCN: 民用化改变了整个地区。

items.example: He changed into civvy after work.

items.exampleCN: 基地之外适用民事规则。

latinEntries.example: Civilien is the direct source of civilian.
latinEntries.exampleCN: civilien 是 civilian 的直接来源。

definition_zh: 装饰品；装饰；勋章
definition_en: something added to make a place look nicer
core_image: 窗台上摆着的一排彩色纸花
scene: 孩子们把纸花贴在窗户上，屋里一下子热闹起来。 Paper decorations hung across the classroom.
sceneCN: 这里 decoration 指「装饰品」（第 1 个义项：加上的好看东西）；句意是纸做的装饰挂满教室。

senses.title: An ornament
senses.definition: an object put somewhere to make it look attractive
senses.definitionCN: 摆放在某处让环境更好看的物件
senses.example: Paper decorations hung across the classroom.
senses.exampleCN: 纸做的装饰挂满了教室。
senses.why: A thing made only to please the eye needs its own name.
senses.whyCN: 只为讨眼睛喜欢而做的东西，需要自己的名字。

senses.title: The act or style of adorning
senses.definition: the work or manner of adding ornaments
senses.definitionCN: 添加饰物的做法或风格
senses.example: The decoration of the hall took two days.
senses.exampleCN: 装饰大厅花了整整两天。
senses.why: The doing and the result are named by one word.
senses.whyCN: 做的过程与做出来的结果，用同一个词称呼。

senses.title: A medal or honour
senses.definition: an official mark of honour given for service
senses.definitionCN: 因功绩而授予的官方荣誉标志
senses.example: He wears the decoration only on formal days.
senses.exampleCN: 他只在正式场合才佩戴这枚勋章。
senses.why: A small pinned object carries a public story.
senses.whyCN: 一枚小小的别针物件，承载着一段公开的故事。

intro.en: Decoration is Latin decoratio, the act of adding beauty or honour, from decorare.
intro.cn: decoration 即拉丁语 decoratio，指添美或添荣的行为，来自 decorare。

items.en: Decoratio named the act of adding beauty or honour.
items.cn: decoratio 指添上美或荣誉的动作。

items.en: The word also came to cover the thing added.
items.cn: 这个词后来也指被添上去的那件东西。

items.en: Décoration meant the adornment of a place.
items.cn: décoration 指对场所的装点。

items.en: Decoration entered English for church and hall ornaments.
items.cn: decoration 进入英语，指教堂与大厅里的饰物。

items.en: It now names medals and interior styles as well.
items.cn: 如今它还指勋章与室内风格。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -ation tail, and the meaning group names ornaments and honours.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -ation 尾，近义组则给出装饰物与荣誉的名称。

entries.definition: a formal public statement
entries.definitionCN: 正式的公开声明

entries.definition: the giving of time and effort to a purpose
entries.definitionCN: 为某个目的付出时间与心力

entries.definition: a group sent to represent others
entries.definitionCN: 被派去代表他人的一群人

entries.definition: an object used to decorate
entries.definitionCN: 用来装饰的物件

entries.definition: something that adds beauty
entries.definitionCN: 增添美感的东西

entries.definition: a metal disc given as an honour
entries.definitionCN: 作为荣誉授予的金属圆牌

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with paper flowers on a window and end with a medal kept in a drawer.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从窗上的纸花开始，落到收在抽屉里的一枚勋章。

normal.en: A decoration is a small thing that changes a whole room.
normal.cn: 一件小小的装饰，能改掉整个房间的气味。

normal.en: Paper flowers are cheap and make the day expensive to forget.
normal.cn: 纸花很便宜，却让那一天贵得忘不掉。

normal.en: Taking decorations down is the saddest part of a party.
normal.cn: 派对最难过的一步，是把装饰取下来。

normal.en: The word covers the doing, the thing and the medal.
normal.cn: 这个词既指动作，也指东西，还指勋章。

normal.en: Honour is pinned on like an ornament, and worn the same way.
normal.cn: 荣誉像饰物一样别在身上，戴法也一模一样。

abstract.en: Picture red paper stuck to cold glass.
abstract.cn: 想象红纸贴在冰冷的玻璃上。

abstract.en: Picture a bare table becoming a party in ten minutes.
abstract.cn: 想象一张空桌子十分钟里变成派对现场。

abstract.en: Picture a medal resting on dark cloth.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚勋章放在深色布面上。

examples.en: Paper decorations hung across the classroom.
examples.cn: 纸做的装饰挂满了教室。

examples.en: The decoration of the hall took two days.
examples.cn: 装饰大厅花了整整两天。

examples.en: She received a decoration for her years of service.
examples.cn: 她因多年服务获得了一枚勋章。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 decoration 记成「得客来省」：de 是得，ration 听着像「来省」，客人来家里，省着点也要把屋里装点一下。

root: 借自拉丁语 decoratio，源头是 decorare（装点），根子为 decus（荣誉与美）。十五世纪进入英语时指教堂与大厅里的饰物，后来既指装饰这个行为与风格，也指挂在胸前的勋章。

sensesIntro.en: From a paper flower on a window, to the work of dressing a hall, to honour worn on a coat.
sensesIntro.cn: 从窗上的一朵纸花，到装点大厅的活儿，再到穿在外套上的荣誉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: paper flowers taped across a window.
core.cn: 核心意象：纸花被一张张贴在窗户上。

branches.en: The first sense is the object itself, made to be seen.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是那件东西本身，生来就是给人看的。

branches.en: The second sense is the work and style behind the object.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是物件背后的手艺与风格。

branches.en: The third sense puts honour where beauty used to be.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把美换成了荣誉。

branches.en: The thing and the doing are one word because they arrive together.
branches.cn: 东西和动作共用一个词，因为它们同时出现。

branches.en: Both are small objects that carry a large meaning.
branches.cn: 两者都是小小的物件，却带着很大的意思。

intro.en: Decoration is the -ion noun of decorate and shares its whole family.
intro.cn: decoration 是 decorate 的名词形式，与整族词共用词干。

latinIntro.en: The root is decus, honour and beauty; decorare gives decorate and decoration.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是 decus（荣誉与美），decorare 长出 decorate 与 decoration。

items.meaning: an ornament or the act of adorning
items.example: The decoration was simple and warm.
The decor matches the old house.
items.exampleCN: 装饰风格与这座老房子很搭。
这些装饰品装满了两个箱子。
没有装饰的房间让人感到安静。
他们重新装修了整间公寓。

definition_zh: 传送；传输；传播；传染；变速器
definition_en: the act of sending something such as signals or power from one place to another, the passing on of disease, or the gear system of a vehicle
core_image: 山脊上的铁塔把看不见的电流送进远处小镇的窗户
scene: 山谷里一座高压铁塔立在山脊上，导线一直伸向远处。 The transmission of power across the valley began last winter.
sceneCN: 这里 transmission 是「传送；传输」（第 1 个义项：把信号、电力等从一处送到另一处）；句意为跨越山谷的电力输送在去年冬天开始运行。铁塔与导线把看不见的东西送到远方，就是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: transmission 的动词形式，义为「传送；传播」
由 transmit 加 -er 构成，义为「发送器；发射台」
由 transmit 加 -ible 构成，义为「可传播的；可传染的」

senses.title: Sending signals or power
senses.definition: the act or process of sending power, signals, or information from one place to another
senses.definitionCN: 把电力、信号或信息从一处送到另一处的行为或过程
senses.example: The transmission of power across the valley began last winter.
senses.exampleCN: 跨越山谷的电力输送在去年冬天开始运行。
senses.why: The Latin parts trans, across, and mittere, to send, say exactly this: sending across.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 parts trans（跨越）与 mittere（送）说的正是这件事：跨越着送出去。

senses.title: Passing on disease
senses.definition: the passing of an infection or a habit from one person or animal to another
senses.definitionCN: 感染或习惯从一人或一动物传给另一人
senses.example: Washing hands reduces the transmission of infection.
senses.exampleCN: 洗手能减少感染的传播。
senses.why: A germ travels from body to body, so the same word covers a crossing that nobody can see.
senses.whyCN: 病菌从一个身体走到另一个身体，于是同一个词容纳了这种看不见的跨越。

senses.title: A broadcast on air
senses.definition: a programme that is sent out by radio or television
senses.definitionCN: 由广播或电视发出的节目
senses.example: The concert was recorded for transmission in the spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这场音乐会被录制下来，准备在春天播出。
senses.why: Signals leave the tower and reach many receivers at once, and the result is called a transmission.
senses.whyCN: 信号离开发射塔同时抵达许多接收机，其结果就叫一次 transmission。

senses.title: The gears of a car
senses.definition: the part of a vehicle that carries power from the engine to the wheels
senses.definitionCN: 车辆中把动力从发动机传到车轮的部件
senses.example: The mechanic found a leak in the transmission.
senses.exampleCN: 修理工发现变速器有渗漏。
senses.why: Mechanical use names the gearbox because its whole job is to transmit turning force.
senses.whyCN: 机械用法把变速箱叫这个名字，因为它全部的职责就是传送转动力。

intro.en: Transmission joins trans, across, with the Latin verb mittere, to send, and its noun missio, a sending.
intro.cn: transmission 由 trans（越过）与拉丁语动词 mittere（送）及其名词 missio（送出）结合而成。

items.en: Mittere meant to send or to let go, a common verb of motion.
items.cn: mittere 意为送出、放走，是常用的运动动词。

items.en: Transmissio named the act of sending something across or through.
items.cn: transmissio 指把某物送过或送穿的动作。

items.en: French passed the word on as transmission, still meaning a crossing over.
items.cn: 法语以 transmission 传出，仍含有穿越之意。

items.en: Early English use concerned the passing on of property or of disease.
items.cn: 英语早期用法涉及财产或疾病的传承。

items.en: With radio and engines the word grew two new homes: broadcasting and gears.
items.cn: 随着无线电与发动机出现，这个词多了两个新家：广播与齿轮箱。

note.en: The first group shares the mit stem, the second holds other words for sending and spreading.
note.cn: 第一组共享 mit 词干，第二组收其他表示发送与扩散的词。

entries.definition: To send signals or pass on disease.
entries.definitionCN: 传送；传播

entries.definition: A device that sends out signals.
entries.definitionCN: 发射机；发送器

entries.definition: Able to be passed from one to another.
entries.definitionCN: 可传播的

entries.definition: A programme sent out to many receivers.
entries.definitionCN: 广播；播出

entries.definition: The act of carrying something.
entries.definitionCN: 运送；传递

entries.definition: A move from one place to another.
entries.definitionCN: 转移；转让

normalIntro.en: Transmission carries the prefix trans and the mission stem, so its spelling tells the whole story of sending across.
normalIntro.cn: transmission 带着前缀 trans 与 mission 词干，拼写本身就讲完了「送过去」的故事。

normal.en: Mission here is not a task but the Latin sending.
normal.cn: 这里的 mission 不是任务，而是拉丁语的「送出」。

normal.en: The plural only adds s: transmissions.
normal.cn: 复数只加 s：transmissions。

normal.en: The stress sits on the second syllable: transMISsion.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节：transMISsion。

normal.en: Transmit is the verb, transmitter is the device that does it.
normal.cn: transmit 是动词，transmitter 是执行它的设备。

normal.en: A car with an automatic transmission shifts gear by itself.
normal.cn: 带自动变速器的车会自己换挡。

abstract.en: A thin wire humming above a valley.
abstract.cn: 山谷上方嗡嗡作响的一根细线。

abstract.en: A voice arriving from a room no one can see.
abstract.cn: 从看不见的房间里传来的声音。

abstract.en: One hand quietly passing a small object to the next.
abstract.cn: 一只手悄悄把一个小东西传给下一只手。

examples.en: The transmission of data between the two offices takes less than a second.
examples.cn: 两个办公室之间的数据传输用时不到一秒。

examples.en: Doctors are studying how the virus spreads from person to person.
examples.cn: 医生们正在研究这种病毒如何在人际间传播。

examples.en: The old truck needs a new transmission before winter.
examples.cn: 这辆旧卡车入冬前需要换新的变速器。

dict_mnemonic.text: trans（越过）＋ mission（送出）——把东西越过距离送出去，就是传输。

root: 拉丁语 transmissio，由 trans（越过）与 mittere（送）的分词词干 miss- 构成，本义「送过去」；同族词有 transmit、transmitter、transmissible。

sensesIntro.en: Power and signals first, then disease, then broadcasting, then the gearbox that carries turning force to the wheels.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是电力与信号，再是疾病，然后是广播，最后是把转动力送到车轮的变速器。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a humming wire over a valley.
core.cn: 核心意象：山谷上方嗡嗡作响的导线。

branches.en: The power branch: energy and data sent across.
branches.cn: 动力分支：被送过去的能量与数据。

branches.en: The illness branch: an infection crossing between bodies.
branches.cn: 疾病分支：感染在身体之间跨越。

branches.en: The broadcast branch: one signal reaching many.
branches.cn: 广播分支：一个信号抵达许多地方。

branches.en: The machine branch: force sent from engine to wheel.
branches.cn: 机械分支：力从发动机送到车轮。

branches.en: The invisible branch: all of it is a sending no eye can follow.
branches.cn: 无形分支：全都是眼睛跟不上的送出。

intro.en: Transmission is built from the prefix trans and the Latin root mit, with the noun ending -ion on top.
intro.cn: transmission 由前缀 trans、拉丁词根 mit 以及名词结尾 -ion 叠加而成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb mittere, to send, supplies the core of the word and of many other English verbs.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语动词 mittere（送）提供了这个词以及许多英语动词的核心。

items.example: It marks the direction of the sending.
The root carries the action of sending.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根承载发送的动作。

items.example: It turns the action into a thing, a transmission.
items.exampleCN: 它把动作变成事物，即一次传输。

items.example: The verb is the bare action.
The device sends the signal out.
items.exampleCN: 这个装置把信号发出去。

items.example: It forms transmissible, able to be passed on.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 transmissible，能被传递的。

items.example: The noun keeps the old sense of being sent.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词保留了「被送出」的古义。

items.example: Sub means under, so the sending goes downward.
items.exampleCN: sub 意为在下，于是送出是朝下的。

items.meaning: to send toward, hence let in
items.example: Ad means to, so the sending goes inward.
items.exampleCN: ad 意为朝向，于是送出是朝内的。

definition_zh: 天文学家
definition_en: a scientist who studies the universe, stars, planets and other celestial bodies
core_image: 一个戴着眼镜、头发花白的老头站在大型望远镜前，抬头望天
scene: 纪录片里解说员说： Edwin Hubble, the astronomer after whom the great telescope was named, proved the universe is expanding.
sceneCN: 这里指「职业是研究天体的科学家」（第1个义项：专业天文学家）；句意为哈勃望远镜命名的那位天文学家证明了宇宙在膨胀。

senses.title: Professional working in the field
senses.definition: a scientist with advanced training in astronomy, employed by observatories, universities or space agencies
senses.definitionCN: 受过高等天文学训练，被天文台、大学或航天机构雇佣的科学家
senses.example: The astronomer stayed up all night collecting data on a rare comet.
senses.exampleCN: 那位天文学家熬夜收集一颗罕见彗星的数据。
senses.why: Like other -er professions, astronomer names the person who does astronomy.
senses.whyCN: 和其他 -er 职业一样，astronomer 就是做 astronomy 的人。

senses.title: Amateur astronomer
senses.definition: a person who observes the sky as a hobby, often with modest equipment but serious enthusiasm
senses.definitionCN: 以观星为爱好的人，设备可能不高级但热情很高
senses.example: An amateur astronomer in Australia spotted a new asteroid before any professional.
senses.exampleCN: 一位澳大利亚业余天文学家比任何职业的都早发现了一颗新小行星。
senses.why: Amateur astronomers can out-professionals when the sky is dark and the target is faint.
senses.whyCN: 业余天文学家能超过职业的，特别是在天空漆黑、目标又暗的时候。

senses.title: Observational vs theoretical
senses.definition: subspecialties: observational astronomers collect data; theoretical astronomers build models
senses.definitionCN: 子专业：观测天文学家收集数据，理论天文学家建立模型
senses.example: She is an observational astronomer who specialises in measuring exoplanet sizes.
senses.exampleCN: 她是专门测量系外行星大小的观测天文学家。
senses.why: Astronomy has the classic split between those who gather evidence and those who explain it.
senses.whyCN: 天文学有经典的分工：收集证据的人和解释证据的人。

senses.title: Historic astronomers
senses.definition: people across cultures who studied the sky before modern science, including Copernicus, Galileo, Kepler, Tycho Brahe
senses.definitionCN: 现代科学之前研究天空的跨文化人物，如哥白尼、伽利略、开普勒、第谷
senses.example: Ancient Arab astronomers gave us most of the star names we still use today.
senses.exampleCN: 古代阿拉伯天文学家给了我们今天仍在使用的大部分星名。
senses.why: Historic astronomers are part of the long tradition that modern astronomy builds on.
senses.whyCN: 历史天文学家是现代天文学所依赖的悠久传统的一部分。

senses.title: Astronomer vs astrophysicist
senses.titleCN: 天文学家 vs 天体物理学家
senses.definition: the boundaries blur; astrophysicists study the physics of celestial objects, astronomers can work in observation or theory broadly
senses.definitionCN: 边界模糊：天体物理学家研究天体物理；天文学家可广泛做观测或理论
senses.example: Many astronomers today are also astrophysicists — the overlap is large.
senses.exampleCN: 今天许多天文学家也是天体物理学家——重叠很大。
senses.why: Both -ist professions share the astron- root, but astrophysicists explicitly study the 'physics' part.
senses.whyCN: 两种 -ist 职业共享 astron- 词根，但 astrophysicist 明确研究 physics 那部分。

senses.title: Astronomer as public scientist
senses.titleCN: 作为公共科学家的天文学家
senses.definition: many astronomers are active science communicators, appearing in documentaries and public talks
senses.definitionCN: 许多天文学家是活跃的科学传播者，出现在纪录片和公共演讲里
senses.example: The astronomer is a regular on late-night science shows.
senses.exampleCN: 这位天文学家是深夜科学节目的常客。
senses.why: Astronomy has broad public appeal — everyone looks up — so astronomers are often the face of science.
senses.whyCN: 天文学有广泛公众吸引力——人人抬头看——所以天文学家常成为科学的脸面。

senses.title: Astronomer at a research facility
senses.titleCN: 科研机构里的天文学家
senses.definition: a staff member of an observatory, space agency or research institute, handling data across projects
senses.definitionCN: 天文台、航天机构或研究所的职员，处理跨项目的数据
senses.example: The observatory employs 12 astronomers to run its flagship telescope.
senses.exampleCN: 这座天文台雇了 12 位天文学家运营它的旗舰望远镜。
senses.why: Big science requires teams, so astronomers work as staff rather than as lone geniuses.
senses.whyCN: 大科学需要团队，所以天文学家是作为职员工作，不是独行天才。

senses.title: Children / dreamers using the word
senses.definition: used informally for anyone fascinated by the sky, not just qualified scientists
senses.definitionCN: 非正式地指任何对天空着迷的人，不只合格科学家
senses.example: As a child I wanted to be an astronomer; now I just look up from the balcony.
senses.exampleCN: 小时候我想当天文学家；现在就从阳台上抬头看看。
senses.why: The word carries wonder, so it's used by dreamers as well as by specialists.
senses.whyCN: 这个词带着浪漫感，所以梦想家和专业人士都用。

intro.en: astronomer adds the English -er agent suffix to astronomy, which itself comes from Greek astron (star) + nomos (law).
intro.cn: astronomer 在 astronomy 上加英语 -er 施事后缀；astronomy 本身来自希腊 astron（星）+ nomos（法）。

items.en: Greek astronomos meant 'one versed in the laws of stars'.
items.cn: 希腊语 astronomos 意为「精通星辰之法的人」。

items.en: Latin astronomus was borrowed directly, meaning 'an astronomer'.
items.cn: 拉丁语直接借入 astronomus，意为「天文学家」。

items.en: Middle English astronomer (14th century) came via Old French astronomier.
items.cn: 中古英语 astronomer（14 世纪）经古法语 astronomier 而来。

items.en: The spelling settled to astronomer, matching astronom- + -er.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 astronomer，对齐 astronom- + -er。

items.en: As astronomy split into subfields, astronomer kept its broad sense while astrophysicist and cosmologist became narrower terms.
items.cn: 当 astronomy 分成子学科时，astronomer 保持广义，而 astrophysicist 和 cosmologist 变得更窄。

items.en: Professional, amateur, historic and popular senses all remain active.
items.cn: 职业、业余、历史、大众的义项今天都仍在使用。

note.en: Group one shares the astron- root with -er / -ist professions; group two are other celestial professionals.
note.cn: 第一组共享 astron- 词根的 -er / -ist 职业；第二组是其他天体领域的专业人士。

entries.definition: General term for someone who studies the sky.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指研究天空的人。

entries.definition: Someone who studies the physics of celestial bodies; subset of astronomer.
entries.definitionCN: 研究天体物理的人；astronomer 的子集。

entries.definition: Astronomer who studies the origin and structure of the whole universe.
entries.definitionCN: 研究整个宇宙起源和结构的天文学家。

entries.definition: Studies life in the universe; not strictly an astronomer.
entries.definitionCN: 研究宇宙中的生命；严格说不算 astronomer。

entries.definition: Flies spacecraft; not a scientist, though many have astronomy backgrounds.
entries.definitionCN: 驾驶航天器的；不是科学家，虽然很多有天文背景。

entries.definition: Uses celestial positions for divination; not a scientist.
entries.definitionCN: 用天体位置占卜；不是科学家。

entries.definition: Bigger category including astronomers, planetary scientists, etc.
entries.definitionCN: 更大的类别，包括天文学家、行星科学家等。

entries.definition: Often an astronomer by training who manages the facility.
entries.definitionCN: 通常是训练有素的天文学家，同时管理天文台。

normalIntro.en: An astronomer is someone who does astronomy.
normalIntro.cn: An astronomer 就是做 astronomy 的人。

normal.en: astronomy + -er = astronomer, just like teacher = teach + -er.
normal.cn: astronomy + -er = astronomer，就像 teacher = teach + -er。

normal.en: Astronomers use telescopes; astrologers use horoscopes.
normal.cn: Astronomers 用望远镜；astrologers 用星盘。

normal.en: Amateur astronomers find comets too — you don't need a PhD.
normal.cn: 业余天文学家也能发现彗星——不一定要博士。

normal.en: Edwin Hubble is the astronomer after whom the telescope is named.
normal.cn: Edwin Hubble 就是哈勃望远镜名字的那位 astronomer。

normal.en: The astronomer stays up all night because the sky is darkest then.
normal.cn: 天文学家熬夜因为那时天空最黑。

abstract.en: A single person in the dark, looking up through glass at light that left a star before the Earth was born.
abstract.cn: 黑暗中的一个人，透过玻璃看着早在地球诞生前就离开恒星的光。

abstract.en: A notebook full of numbers, a red headlamp, cold coffee at 3am.
abstract.cn: 一本写满数字的笔记本、红色头灯、凌晨三点的冷咖啡。

abstract.en: Tiny, alone, and looking upward out of sheer habit.
abstract.cn: 微小、孤独、纯粹出于习惯地向上看。

examples.en: The astronomer's paper on black hole imaging won the biggest prize in physics that year.
examples.cn: 这位天文学家关于黑洞成像的论文那年拿了物理领域最大的奖。

examples.en: My cousin is an amateur astronomer who drives to the desert every new moon.
examples.cn: 我表弟是业余天文学家，每个新月都开车去沙漠。

examples.en: Astronomers from 20 nations collaborated to build the Event Horizon Telescope.
examples.cn: 20 个国家的天文学家合作建了事件视界望远镜。

dict_mnemonic.text: astronomy（天文学）+ -er（做...的人）= 天文学家

root: 希腊语 astron（星）+ nomos（法则）→ astronomy → 加 -er 指「做…的人」→ astronomer。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses describe who astronomers are: professional, amateur, observational, theoretical, historic, boundary-vs-astrophysicist, public communicators, and dreamers.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项讲 astronomer 是谁：职业的、业余的、观测的、理论的、历史上的、与天体物理学家的边界、公共传播者、梦想家。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lone figure at a telescope eyepiece, lit only by a faint red lamp and the stars overhead.
core.cn: 核心意象：目镜前一个孤独的身影，只有微弱红灯和头顶的星光照着。

intro.en: astronomer is astronomy + -er; the -er suffix turns a science name into the person who practises it.
intro.cn: astronomer 就是 astronomy + -er；-er 后缀把一门科学变成做它的人。

latinIntro.en: The astron- root is Greek; -er is English but has Latin cognate -or (as in actor).
latinIntro.cn: astron- 来自希腊；-er 是英语但有拉丁同源 -or（如 actor）。
